1159 Burn’s Sleep, Nascent realm
In Deadhouse Gates, the group (Felisin, Heboric, Baudin, Kulp, Gesler, Stormy, Truth) were aboard the ship Ripath while fleeing from an unnamed insane mage who pulled them into the Nascent realm
The Nascent is a warren of a plain that's been flooded
A three to four story high wall holds back floodwater protecting a city whose roofs could be seen peeking over the wall
The silts of the plain creates a beach shoreline against the wall
Corpses of the warren’s inhabitants wash up on the shoreline
The inhabitants were short, squat, flat featured, had long pale hair, and wore thick padded clothing for the cold weather in the Nascent, being eaten by coin-sized black crabs
For months, a freshwater river large enough to span a continent had been flowing into the Nascent through a rent. The rent closed the night before the HoC prologue starts
Trull Sengar is being escorted by his kin to be shorn, excommunicated and existence erased by his people
Trull Sengar spoke against their leader, claiming he served a hidden master and defended their enemies, claiming they were ‘Pure Kin’
Trull’s kin shackles Trull against the wall, carves a circle with a slash through it, and rubs an unguent that makes him bald
Trull believes that Nature’s only enemy is imbalance which his brother shattered, Trull along with his people will drown
Book One:
The Faces in the Rock
Unknown centuries in the past
A loyal tribe dog goes rabid, kills some Uryd tribe people, the Uryd tribe corners it into a kiln to kill it
A father carries his child to die and be sacrificed to the Seven Faces in the Rock, the Seven Gods of the Teblor
Chapter 1 Scene 2 (Faces in the Rock, Karsa)
1159 Burn’s Sleep
In a glade, Karsa Orlong bows and prays before the Faces in the Rock and admires his grandfather Pahlk Orlong, a proud Teblor raider and warrior
Karsa hates his father, Synyg Orlong for being a pacifist even though he’s a skilled warrior
The Uryd clan descended from Urugal the Woven, the fiercest of the seven gods, but are now complacent and passive
There are six Teblor clans dedicated to each of the seven gods, Siballe the Unfound lacks a tribe

Karsa Orlong vows that he and his two friends, Bairoth Gild and Delum Thord, will reclaim glory to the Uryd clan by following his grandfather Pahlk’s footsteps to raid rival Teblor clans and Silver Lake, a legendary village, two weeks away from the Uryd territory
Karsa also fantasizes about a girl, Dayliss, who is not interested in him
Karsa, 80 years old and adolescent in Teblor years, hopes to be the one to unite the Teblor clans to start the War of the People
Seven broken bodies of the Faces in the Rock rise from the ground
They were too shattered to follow their kin
Their failure had not been honourable, thus entombed in darkness instead of remained placed where they could see open skies and vistas
To be free they have to break their vows and swear fealty to another (gee I wonder who tf this is)
The Seven Faces in the Rock
Urual, “Mossy Bone”, Teblor known as Urugal
Sin’b’alle, “Lichen for Moss”, Sinballe the Unfound
Ber’ok, “Dead Ash Tree”
Haran’alle, “Antler from Summer”
Thek Ist, “Spear Leg”
Emroth, “Fanged Skeleton”
Kahlb, “Red Moss”
Urugal believes Karsa will be the one to free them
Karsa’s grandfather Pahlk’s raid on Silver Lake wasn't enough. ‘Sundering the vow’ took too much of their power, and their new master barely gave them some
The Teblor don't know their real name
Karsa returns to his father’s home and finds him grooming Havok
Synyg tells Karsa his companions wait for him at the ford, that Dayliss blessed Bairoth, and that he wouldn't bless Karsa because he hates violence and believe the Seven Faces in the Rock are a lie
Says grandfather Pahlk’s blessing was self-serving
Four bloodposts marking Karsa’s siblings sacrificed to the Seven Faces in the Rock lead towards the village
Synyg didn't decorate the bloodposts and Karsa thought his siblings deserved better and will make them proud
Karsa meets up with Bairoth Gild and Delum Thord, they all tease each other
Karsa insults Dayliss, Bairoth Gild confronts Karsa and says they're going to marry when they return. Karsa challenges Bairoth, Bairoth backs off
The three warriors depart
The village elder’s were against the journey so only Dayliss watched them leave
‘Lead us, Warleader, into glory.’
23 Uryd spirits, the sacrificed children to the seven Faces in the Rock, watch Karsa depart
The spirits were Siballe the Unfound’s secret tribe, called the Found
Some people like Karsa’s father Synyg suspected the Found spirits existed
Some were siblings to the three warriors
Siballe scarred the Found by stripping flesh and muscle from the left side of their faces, diminishing their ability for facial expressions and inflections in their voice
Words of hope would sound like lies even to themselves
Chapter 1 Scene 6 (Synyg’s House, Synyg)
Pahlk comes to Synyg’s house to yell at his son for not blessing Karsa’s journey
Synyg gave Havok to Karsa so that at least the horse can experience one last battle of glory that Synyg would not give him
Synyg cooked supper for the both of them
When finished, Synyg picked up his father and threw him out of his house, saying that he'd kill him if he tried to come inside again
The Uryd trio stealth through rival Teblor lands, though Karsa wanted to carve a bloody war path
Bairoth and Delum urge their horses need rest, Karsa reluctantly agrees and made camp
Delum Thord catches rabbits and they eat them raw because they can't make a campfire or risk being caught
Raw meat was known to carry diseases fatal to the Teblor, but no one became ill again when the Faces in the Rock appeared
Delum and Bairoth think night is safer for them to travel, Karsa as warleader says they will continue to travel by day while their horses can see and walk more confidently
Bairoth and Karsa argue about wisdom, Bairoth reassures the two warriors trust their war leader, and believe the Teblor elders will lie and say how they blessed the warriors all along
Chapter 1 Scene 8 (Rathyd camp, Karsa)
The Uryd trio find a Rathyd camp of 8 who just hunted a grey bear, and a ninth Rahyd youth (at 40 years old)
3 Rathyd were eating bear meat, 2 were rubbing blood oil on their swords, the last 3 standing at the trail near the camp
Karsa’s bloodwood sword is deep red, nearly black, with a glassy polish of the blood-oil that repaired damage
Karsa charges in first expecting Bairoth and Delum to follow up and attack
Karsa charges in and kills 7, Bairoth and Delum kill the 8th, the Rathyd youth was able to flee
Bairoth is angry that Karsa let the youth escape and will grow up to be a warleader
Karsa vows the youth will be Rathyd warleader that kneels before him
‘One vow along many I have made. And each shall be kept. Witness, if you dare.’
The Uryd trio splits the Rathyd trophies from the grey bear
The Uryd trio slaughter another Rathyd adult and two youths before camping for the night
Karsa plans to instigate a war between the Rathyd and Sunyd tribes
Slaughter a Rathyd village and be chased into Sunyd lands, the Sunyd would think they’re being invaded
Bairoth messes with the bear skull, too heavy to wear as a helmet and the warriors sleep for the night
Chapter 1 Scene 10 (Rathyd Village, Karsa)
The three Uryd warriors slaughter the Rathyd village
After the slaughter is complete, the women are herded to the village center and choose who they would rape
The village chief’s wife says the women they chose were eager, which confuses Karsa
The chief’s implies Teblor women have desires of rival Teblor men and makes Karsa doubt that the women of his own Uryd tribe would not do the same
She recognizes Pahlk’s name and says that he was basically a little bitch that begged them to let him through
Karsa hears moaning of pleasure from the Bairoth/Delum’s huts, Karsa is unsettled that they are not being raped (lmfao)
Karsa is pissed calls for the three to “rape” all the women in the village
While with the chief’s daughter, he calls her Dayliss and tells her to raise his children as Uryd
Rathyd hunting parties and a dog pack chase the Uryd trio
The Uryd trio make camp, Bairoth fashions the bear skull into a giant bolas weapon
Bairoth Gild remains at the camp, Karsa and Delum Thord head towards the dog pack
Traveling over moss to dampen their noise, they sit and wait on the slope for the dog pack’s arrival
The dog pack appears, Karsa finds the leader and pins the dog, left hand on his neck and right hand holding both front legs
One younger dog, whom Karsa figured was the leader’s rival, is instantly killed by Delum’s knife throws
Karsa manages to bring the dog pack under submission and they now follow him
Delum Thord is impressed and now believes in Karsa’s journey, ‘I am witness to this.’ ✨
Karsa says his goal is to have all Teblor kneel before him, the journey to Silver Lake is only a scouting mission to see their future enemy
Karsa names the lead dog Gnaw
The Uryd trio and dog pack continue traveling a hunting track downhill into a valley
Karsa is pissed the rival Rathyd clan aren’t chasing after them
At the bottom of the valley they find a wooden walkway buried in the mud with trees sunk to chest level
Karsa talks about how his grandfather Pahlk and the Teblor elders went to investigate the ice melting at the Buryd Fissure 60 years ago. The sound of the ice melting was heard across the Teblor lands
Pahlk and the Teblor elders found frozen beasts, crushed ivory, a black heart, signs of ancient battle, bones of children, broken stone weapons
Rathyd warriors appear on both in front and behind the Uryd trio
Delum and Bairoth deal with the 6 in front while Karsa deals with the 8 in the back
Bairoth swung his bear skull bolas and threw it, crushing the Rathyd horse’s chest
The injured horse stomped the horse beside it, kicking it off the path and its rider fell off (1💀
The Rathyd rider fell to the feet of Bairoth and was stomped to death by his horse (2💀
The horse charge fails, one horse trips and falls over the first dead horse. Bairoth charges forward to kill its rider with his bloodsword (3💀
Delum appears behind Bairoth and kills another Rathyd with two knife throws, the first parried and the second hits his throat (4💀
Bairoth and Delum duel the remaining two riders (5 & 6💀
Karsa, on Havok with the dog pack flanking him, faces the dozen Rathyd warriors behind them
8 adults form an inverted V formation as the 4 youths are sent down either side of the wooden path
Karsa charges the V-formation’s left, parries an attack, and hack and slashes his way through the center (a la Dynasty Warriors)
The dog pack attacks the Rathyd warriors, their former tribe
Two warriors escape from the dog pack and flees with the four youths
Bairoth and Delum appear to finish off the Rathyds that escaped
Gnaw and five other dogs remain, one dog missing a leg
Karsa tells Delum to bind and cauterize the missing leg, says the dog will lie peacefully at his hearth when they return home
Karsa gains the respect of Havok and Bairoth ✨
‘I am content to follow you, Warleader.’ You ever were, Bairoth Gild, and that is the difference between us.
17th or 18th Jaghut War of the Kron T'lan Imass (the same clan as Pran Chole) was a failure

Pran Chole: Bonecaster that aided in Kruppe’s dream to reincarnate Tattersail as Silverfox and guided Itkovian in taking the T’lan Imass’ suffering. Left to Assail with SilverFox at the end of Memories of Ice
A Jaghut still survived in the Laederon glacier
Shattered malformed remains of T’lan Imass with Omtose Phellack (Jaghut) sorcery on them and broken weapons remained in the glacier
Surviving T’lan Imass survivors took the Kron ensorcelled weapons away with them
For reference, all other Jaghut Wars mentioned thus far in the series
6th Jaghut War: where Onos T’oolan was whetted as a warrior (Gardens of the Moon)
28th Jaghut War: where the Taran clan met their end, Tool becoming the final survivor (Gardens of the Moon)
33rd Jaghut War: Right before the Ritual of Tellann, when the T’lan Imass hunted the Jaghut mother and her two children, which went on to become the Pannion Seer (Memories of Ice prologue)
The Rathyd hunting group stopped pursuing the Uryd trio, possibly left to warn the other villages
Karsa plans to sneak past the valleys and attack the last Rathyd village leading them into Sunyd territory
Karsa realizes the three legged dog is Gnaw’s mate, happy he didn't put her down
The path leads uphill, the Uryd trio find a cave near the hill summit with a cairn of piled stones and Teblor bloodsigns scribed on the walls, more ornate than their language
The writer led families down from the highlands through glaciers
T’lan Imass were close by (unknown to the Uryd trio)
The writer split up families to create new families isolated from each other, proclaiming the Laws of Isolation which Icarium (?!) bestowed to save them
The writer's people sheltered Icarium, Icarium was heartbroken to see what the people became

‘To survive we must forget,we must dismantle our [unknown word] and burn our [unknown word] and leave naught but ash. We must forget our history and seek only our most ancient of legends. We must return to those terrible times, to isolate out streams of blood. New threads must be born of rape, for only violence would they remain rare occurrences, and random. To cleanse our blood, we must forget all that we were, yet find what we had once been’
Named the tribes after his brothers
Baryd, Sanyd, Phalyd, Urad, Gelad, Manyd, Rathyd, and Lanyd
The rest of the passage is too dark to read
Karsa doesn't want to read anymore
A dark fissure is seen deeper in the cave, the warriors guess the writer crawled and died inside
Two nights pass, the Uryd trio reach Sunyd territory
The Rathyd villages were abandoned, so none pursued and Karsa's plan to incite a war fails
The Sunyd villages are also abandoned, Karsa decides to raid Silver Lake
The group travels to the bottom of the valley. No longer needing to hide, they hunt and cook hares for the first time on the journey
Bairoth mentions talking to Delum about the cave writings
Urad too close to Uryd, tales of tribes that existed more before than now
The two words Karsa couldn't read that Delum inferred: we must dismantle our [great villages] and burn our [yellow bark] and leave naught but ash.’ The Teblor language used to be more complex
Delum points out their tales of glory now appear to be instructions, codes of behavior, the proper way of being a Teblor

Delum figures the Teblor were a defeated people, brothers and sisters born with defects of inbreeding (that they understand from inbred dogs and horses: too many fingers and toes, mouths with no palates, faces with no eyes)
The Teblor elder of the cave knew what threatened the Teblor, separated the race “to clear them of cloudy blood”, the cave a scene of an ancient crime
Karsa remains adamant about continuing his mission to unite the tribes to fight the lowlanders

Bairoth believes defeat of the Teblor will come again, teases Karsa's self confidence, believes Pahlk's raids of Silver Lake were false, and that Karsa’s father Synyg is to be respected. Hopes that Karsa can learn wisdom from the feeling of uncertainty
Karsa feels threatened and challenges Bairoth, Bairoth submits to Karsa, only to stop the pointless duel
The Teblor warriors reach a Sunyd village long abandoned that were raided by raiders from Silver Lake
Brambles and nature reclaimed the village, trails leading into the village are covered
Karsa now wages war against the people of Silver Lake for the sake and honor of all Teblor
Leaving the village, the trail brings them into the forest that led into the side of the valley
The warriors camp at the summit, finding a high walled cul-de-sac
Karsa follows Gnaw and his three legged mate head into another dead end, the dogs are afraid and scurry away
In another dead end, a large slightly glowing slab of rock pins down what Delum thinks is a Forkassal
Only a hand with milky blue green skin, long slender joints with too many joints, was visible outside the slab, claw marks all around it
Bairoth recalls the Teblor tale of the Spirit Wars
Two to three invasions, foreign gods and demons, only one force remained
The only known mention of Icarium is in those tales
The T’lan Imass that wrote in the cave may have been a part of the Spirit Wars
The Spirit Wars may have split the Teblor into tribes
The Forkassal, ‘the One who Sought Peace’, came to make peace between the contestants
Icarium came for the same reason but was too late and gave the Teblor the Laws of Isolation
Speculation: The Spirit Wars may be the same 17th/18th Jaghut War of the Kron T’lan Imass
Bairoth wishes to free the Forkassal under the rock
Karsa sees the magic in the slab weakening
The Teblor only knew sorcery after the Seven appeared, and only in their dreams
Bairoth and Delum argue before Karsa makes the decision to free the Forkassal
When the boulder was lifted, they saw an elongated figure laying on its side covered in spiderwebs
Elongated limbs, extra-jointed, skin stretched taut and pallid as moonlight, blue-black hair spread across the ground latticed like roots. This figure was naked and female
The Forkassal stood up slowly and shakily, hair crumbling into dust until she was bald
Flawless skin like polished marble, broad brow, midnight eyes flat and dry like onyx under a layer of dust, high flaring cheekbones, wide mouth crusted with fine crystals (dehydration, not a feature)
Body a mass of planes and angles, breasts high and far apart, sternum prominent in between, too many ribs, tall as a Teblor child
Karsa tells Bairoth not to touch her because she might not want to be touched ever again
Bairoth is grateful and impressed that Karsa freed the Forkassal
Karsa sees the Forkassal make a weak smile and believes it to be embarrassment for her condition. Karsa vows to Urugal that he will seek vengeance against the T’lan Imass
The Teblor warriors introduce themselves and try to talk to the Forkassal and see that she is immediately recovering
The Forkassal half smiles at them in understanding and immediately attacks Karsa
Karsa was hit five times instantly and woke up on the floor
Delum cried out, Forkassal stands over Karsa,  Bairoth begs to leave him
The Forkassal, now with full purple lips, speaks to Karsa in the Teblor language
Her former enemies won't leave the Teblor alone, shattering their bones wasn't enough
She will wait to see what the Teblor will do before deciding to give them eternal peace
(ah, peace means death)
Her name is Calm, a Bringer of Peace and Forkrul Assail
The Teblor have also twisted the true name of their people
Icarium and T’lan Imass imprisoned her, is aware of Icarium’s poor memory, and the T’lan Imass are far away
Out of gratitude for freeing her, Calm says Karsa has been chosen
If the Tebor knew his ultimate purpose they would kill him, but those that chose him would simply choose another
Calm tells his companions ‘there will come a time when he stands poised to change the world’
When that time comes, she will be there to bring peace. Calm walks away
Bairoth Gild regrets freeing her and is ashamed that he did not unsheathe his weapon to defend them
Karsa tells him that was the right thing to do because at least one of them is healthy
Delum’s forehead was split with yellow liquid oozing out of the pierced bone and clear fluid (cerebrospinal fluid), eyes wide and cloudy with confusion, parts of his face slack
They wrap Delum’s head in bandages, finds the dogs huddled frightened together, and Forkrul Assail footprints leading south
Delum Thord’s mental state is reduced to a dog and he becomes part of Gnaw’s dog pack
Bairoth feels guilty for freeing the Forkrul Assail and Delum’s condition
Karsa doubles down in his mind that Bairoth was correct in not facing a more powerful opponent, Delum made his mistake and now paid the consequence while Bairoth is self-indulging in grief
The Uryd trio continue traveling and take a rest
Bairoth returns with a goat, Gnaw and his mate take first pick of the meat before the dogs and Delum eat
Karsa jokes that Gnaw’s pack has grown by one which upsets Bairoth
Bairoth is upset that Karsa won't reveal what the Forkrul Assail
whispered to him and no longer stands by Karsa
Karsa reasserts his superiority over Bairoth
Bairoth says that even if Karsa returns and forces Dayliss to be his wife, he will always behind Bairoth for her love
Karsa says he doesn't want to wife Dayliss anymore, rather to denounce her from the tribe for adultery and making her his slave
Bairoth charges at Karsa, one arm around his neck and his knife hand cutting Karsa’s chest
Gnaw and the dogs charge at Bairoth, forcing him away from Karsa, Karsa then shoos the dogs away
Karsa and the dogs are alerted to “lowlanders” nearby and they all stealth to the shadows, Bairoth readies himself but Karsa forced him to withdraw
A party of nine “lowlanders” enter the cul-de-sac
Two armored guards stood watch at entrance, four robed figures had hair braided to their chest, three scouts in leather wielded shortbows and have clan tattoos
Karsa charged and beheaded one of the armored guards and blocked the only exit out if the cul-de-sac
One scout charged and is immediately crushed by Karsa’s bloodwood sword, the other two scouts slashed at Karsa’s ribs from the side
Karsa swings and crushes the second scout’s skull, then backswings and sends the third scout flying to collide with the wall
The robed figures chant and confidently cast fire to engulf Karsa
Karsa shrugs it off, which freaks out the mages and Karsa kills them
Bairoth says the dogs are hunting the second guard that escaped and comments that the “lowlanders” are like babes
Now we understand that the Teblor consider all humans as “children” since they’re the size of Teblor newborns, and all readers breathe a sigh of relief
Karsa makes Bairoth agree to put their argument aside until they deal with the “lowlanders”
The guard escapes
Gnaw’s dog pack returned at sunrise with two less dogs, Delum carries Gnaw’s three legged mate
Karsa collects ears and tongues as trophies on a leather necklace
By noon, the Uryd duo found the two dead dogs, killed by crossbow bolts, and pieces of armor the guard shed off as he escaped
Karsa decides to not pursue the escaped guard and continue to Bone Pass
The Uryd duo travel uphill, reaching clouds of mist, until they reach a sheer drop where it looks like the mountain was cut by an axe. Thin waterfalls leaking to the valley below

Karsa threw a rock to the narrow cliffside trail that caused a landslide and revealed a larger path, made of bones. Lowlander-sized but heavier and thicker, some with antlers and tusks, and helms made from larger beasts
Note: Guess whose bones these are?
The group descended into the dark gloom a thousand steps to a leveled shelf where the river roared next to them before dropping into the valley below
Karsa wants to continue, noticing that rocks continue to fall down and wary that the escaped guard may cause a rockslide to bury Karsa and co.

The group continues to descend, hearing another natural rockslide behind them, another thousand steps to reach another shelf where the bones are buried in mud, completing the passage through Bone Pass

Bairoth is distraught that they will have to climb this on the way back, Karsa plans instead to travel entirely through lowlander territory and the Laederon Plateau and discover hidden passes that lowlanders use to reach Uryd lands
The Bone Pass slope led to a damp forest of redwoods and cedars
The group rests on bedrock exposed at the base of a fallen and uprooted cedar tree
Karsa explains they are on the south side of the river that leads to Silver Lake, with a spar of rock between them and the southwestern village
Karsa agrees to Bairoth’s plea to attack in daylight
After four days’ travel through the forest the group nears Silver Lake

Bairoth believes the recent tracks on the trail belonged to the lowlanders they killed and wonder if they worshipped the Forkrul Assail like the Teblor worship the Seven Faces in the Rock, also recognizing their sorcery was god-aspected
Bairoth thinks the dead that made Bone Pass were those that imprisoned the Forkrul Assail and were kin to the “lowlanders”, but Karsa doesn’t care or want to talk about it

In the middle of the night, Karsa catches Bairoth painting the battle mask on Delum meant for old warriors fighting until they die and calls it dishonorable to the Uryd because Delum doesn’t understand
Bairoth finds no glory in fighting and believes Delum holds on to the three legged dog because he seeks comfort
Karsa and Bairoth begin moving on the pebbled beach towards the farm and the town
Bairoth cries a warning, but Karsa ignores it and charges, beheading one farmer and trampling another farmer woman
The town rings alarm bells and closes its gates
Havok, being twice the height of a normal horse, hurdles over the town’s wall easily and lands on a chicken coop
Karsa kills a villager curiously looking out his door and then charges against the guards locking the gate with a plank, cutting down and trampling six lowlanders
Unable to figure out the metal latches, Karsa got off his horse and shoulder tackled the gate, toppling it forward and collapsing the guard towers at the side
Bairoth, Delum, and the dogs enter the town. Delum appeared to have torn out the neck of a farmer with his bare teeth like a dog

A group of thirty pikemen arrive. Karsa charges on Havok taking up their view, upon hearing Bairoth’s roar Karsa veers to the side as Bairoth’s giant grey bear skull is thrown crushing the formation, allowing the dogs and the Teblor to slaughter them all
A group of fifty to sixty soldiers appeared at the gate, with twenty in plate armor and on horseback
Karsa leads his group through a side street leading them to the lake shoreline, where a pile of Teblor bones and skulls on poles stood as a monument
Among the tents and huts on the shoreline emerged people wearing Teblor scalps and fetishes
In fear and rage, Bairoth charged. Their arrows took down his horse and Bairoth falls to the ground

Karsa parries a bronze axe with his bloodsword. With his left hand he grabs an axe aiming for Havok’s neck, rips it from the lowlander and tosses it away. Then he grabs and crushes the lowlander’s neck and tosses his corpse
Havok takes a pike to its chest, and topples to the ground bleeding out

Karsa leaps off Havok, slaps away a sword and lands on three lowlanders, crushing them. Standing up he slashes a man’s bearded jaw off and spins to impale another soldier slashing Karsa’s back behind him
A crescent line of archers and crossbowmen launch a volley at Karsa, a handful hitting him
Karsa charges the line and cuts down eight, laughing all the while
Karsa tried to follow the sound of Gnaw’s pack, finding a string of bodies before the dogs all were killed themselves

Delum was found shrieking, impaled with a javelin and a dozen quarrels crawling to where a mob was beating Gnaw’s three legged mate to death. A figure comes out of the alley and crushes Delum’s skull with a shovel, Delum Thord is dead

Karsa cut Delum’s slayer in half, killed several of the mate’s slayers, and ran to where Gnaw was on the other side of the street and picked him up to chase after a mattock-wielding (farm pickaxe) villager that escaped across a sewage ditch, through some woods, into a barn
Karsa sets Gnaw on a straw pile to rest and prays to Urugal to help Gnaw find his way to the Uryd tribe
Karsa pulls and snaps the quarrels in his body, climbs chains up to a platform above, finds the mattock-lowlander crying to himself below
Karsa does a plunging attack with his bloodwood sword and kills the mattock-lowlander, breaking the floor and falling further down into a cellar
Karsa is impaled by a piece of wood through his chest and lost his bloodwood sword
Lowlanders circle around the hole in the floor, and a tattooed man speaks with Karsa in the Sunyd Teblor dialect
The man heard Pahlk’s name and clarified Pahlk reached Silver Lake half-starved, nursed back to health by farmers, which he then killed and fled. A girl survived and escaped south to Orbs.

When the duo return to the tower, Keeper throws them a bag of silver jakatas and local currency of high denomination
Keeper arranged his own death and emptied half of Aren’s treasury before his ‘drowning’ ready to keep his anonymity
The duo part ways and head to Ehrlitan

cards.h: ‘I will see to it that you find a ship, so that you may return to your family. I shall, however, keep the truth of your friendship with me’

i.html: ‘Without you and your endless words, Torvald Nom, the madness I had feigned
would have become a madness in truth… I had followers, but not allies, and only
now do I understand the difference. And it is vast. And from this, I have come to
understand what it is to possess regrets. Bairoth Gild. Delum Thord. Even the
Rathyd whom I have greatly weakened. When I return to my old path, back into the
lands of the Teblor, there are wounds that I shall need to mend. And so, when you
say it is time to return to your family, Torvald Nom, I understand and my heart is
gladdened.’
Four days passed, the duo crossed five villages along the coastal road
Karsa overheard in Genabaris that Seven Cities was about to rebel and comments that’s why the Teblor never conquer, so they can continuously raid
Torvald comments on the imperial way, that Seven Cities was known to be a rat’s nest for civil wars leading to the suffering and misery of its people while warlords and corrupt priest-kings reign.
With the Malazan conquest: thugs were executed, tribes stopped raiding, and the priesthoods were destroyed.
Though the merchants are richer or safe, thus likely to be in rebellion.
Hatred is found everywhere. Opinions becomes conviction, and with anger and fear people become less rational and only violence and death remains
The duo come to a sixth village, walking the empty street until about 36 Arak tribal horsemen appear at the front and 20 from behind
A year ago Karsa would’ve charged, instead he sheaths his weapon knowing the futility in resisting
Shackles are placed once again on the duo, small enough to cut off Karsa’s circulation
Silgar and Damisk appear, hiring the Arak tribe to get revenge for the death of his men and arrest
Karsa is knocked down to his knees and clubbed in the head, which he answers by taking the Arak’s chains and whipping him in the face
Karsa iss mobbed by clubs and beaten unconscious
Karsa wakes up in a travois, the Arak made camp with a city visible in the horizon
Torvald rips off his and Karsa’s shirt, fills it with piles of grass.
Then he places them in the Arak’s smokeless fires that kept them undetected, the shirt and grasses roared in flames which attract the attention of a nearby enemy tribe, the Gral
The night is in chaos as the Gral approach, one tribesman slit Torvald Nom’s throat for causing the fire
The slayer reaches for his horse,  instantaneously he and his two companions are silently decapitated
Silgar defends himself with a wave of sorcery that knocks a Gral to the ground, crackling his body until his flesh explodes
Damisk cuts Karsa’s ropes free from its travois, Silgar transports them to ‘fetid warm water’ and then a second time to empty city streets
Karsa doesn’t have official Malazan slave brands, so Damisk removes his chains and Silgar unleashes a wave of sorcery that makes Karsa scream
Malazan guards come and Silgar feigns he’s an escaped slave
Karsa wakes to hear a Malazan healer (Scrawl) inspecting his incredible regeneration, thinking he’s Fenn (giants from Li Heng that’s been unseen for decades)
When the Malazans leave, a fellow inmate informs Karsa that Silgar and Damisk were arrested for keeping an unsanctioned slave without the proper brand
They also confessed Karsa was on his way to the otataral mines, and his “curse” killed a shipworth of Malazans
Silgar was chained with an otataral shackle and won’t be able to cast sorcery
Karsa asks what otataral is and says the Teblor scrape a similar red powder from cliff sides to make their blood-oil
The prisoner warns not to share that with anyone. Since the mines are thought to be the only source of otataral in the world and impossible to conquer without the help of the T’lan Imass
Malazans enter, the prisoner stands revealing he is lean, tan, and has light blue eyes. The prisoner is denied a trial, as he was connected to a secret organization where a traitor ratted him out
Soldiers Jibb and Gullstream (white blotches on a high forehead) stays to keep watch over Karsa, and they remark on Scrawl’s shattered slave brand on Karsa’s face
The prisoner is escorted out to be chained a part of a prison line
Jibb and Gullstream mention the Ashok Regiment are arriving as reinforcements for the rebellion while Red Blades are stirring up further trouble
Karsa is taken out and chained to the prisoner line, his position next to the light blue eyed prisoner
The native prisoner suggests a partnership in the mines to survive, which Karsa accepts
Karsa falls asleep when night falls. The native prisoner wakes him up and the Malazan compound is emptiy of guards
Two cloaked figures walk to Karsa, Torvald Nom pulls his robe back
The Gral takes prisoners and has a partnership with the House of Nom to broker and sell them
Torvald decides to be one of the Gral for the unique experience before he returns home
Torvald retrieved and gives Karsa his bloodwood sword, as the Gral kill the remaining prisoners in the line one-by-one just because they don’t like them
The native prisoner persuades them that he can take Karsa to safety, Torvald leaves with the Gral
The native prisoner takes Karsa’s through alleyways to a tower on top of the hill, where he calls for Mebra
Mebra lets them inside and is sworn to keep their escape a secret, even among their organization
The duo enters the tower and descends stairs into tunnels deep, deep below. Travel supplies and weapon caches are dispersed in niches at regular intervals
Karsa ponders on his life outside the Teblor, how there were so many tribes in the world obsessed with their differences but no focus on what unified them.
A flaw Karsa figursd he could exploit
The tunnels exits to a gully. They are five to six days travel across the Pan’potsun Odhan to the prisoner’s next destination and he knows the route that contains all the locations with fresh water
[DG Chapter 2 Scene 4]
Mebra was Kalam Mekhar’s contact in Seven Cities and gives him the Holy Book of Dryjnha, stolen from High Fist Pormqual’s vaults in Aren
Mebra tasked Kalam to deliver the book to Sha’ik and initiate the Whirlwind Rebellion
Mebra was also a double agent with the Red Blades (Seven Cities natives that are loyal to the Malazan Empire) and this scheme was meant to find Sha’ik and kill her
The scheme was a success, Kalam led the Red Blades directly to Sha’ik and they killed her
Karsa and the native prisoner climbs out of the gully as the sun rises, traveling in silence
In the afternoon, the native senses at least 20 horsemen with a mage are approaching and confirms his suspicion that Mebra is a traitor
Karsa states by night time, he’ll turn and fight them even if he fights alone
At night, the duo see there are 15 fully armored horseman, Silgar, Damisk, and three spare horses
Karsa recalls that they must’ve escaped by the time the Gral broke them out of the compound
The horsemen make camp, and Karsa finds it to be the opportunity to approach
Karsa remembers his time with the Ashok Regiment, the soldiers spent time replacing their crossbow cords, tending to their horses, and setting up a cooked meals
Karsa stealths and takes cover behind a boulder, then instantly rushes the picket guards, crushing the first one’s windpipe and decapitating a second soldier. The camp is alerted
A brave soldier attacks first to buy time for his companions to shield themselves, Karsa severs both his arms. The shields are useless as Karsa crashes his bloodwood sword on the next two soldiers
A lance pierces his right thigh, Karsa parries a second thrown lance
Silgar casts a wave of sorcery just as a picket guard rushes to attack Karsa
The picket guard screams in pain until death, as Karsa brushes the sorcery off and heads directly towards Silgar
Karsa cuts off Silgar’s hands, then his right ankle, then his left foot
A command is shouted in the air and the Malazans retreat
Karsa picks up Silgar by the belt and walks away from the camp, the native prisoner is nearby
The native tells him to leave or Silgar who’s leaving a blood trail
To the native’s dismay, Karsa cuts off pieces of Silgar’s telaba to tie around his stumps and wants to prolong his pain and drive him mad before killing him
‘Lead us on, lowlander’
Eight days pass, they reach a hidden pass through the mountains and successfully evaded the pursuing Malazans
At a plain near the summit Karsa looks over the desert ahead of them
The native is appalled that the Teblor don’t remember their true name as Thelomen Toblakai
They existed while the T’lan Imass were still flesh, before the Ritual of Tellann
The barghast and trell descended from the Thelomen Toblakai
The native reveals himself to be Leoman, and he serves to deliver Karsa to Sha’ik in the heart of Raraku
Book Two:
Cold Iron
Commander Blistig kicks down an [unlocked] door of an inn, his Aren Guard enters to retrieve a unkempt, broken-hearted Squint. Fist Gamet follows
Aren’s port only has a few Malazan warships and transports, ‘a scarred populace’
Fist Gamet is concerned about inheriting the Chain of Dogs survivors, shocked by the lack of ‘military decorum’

Blistig blows up in his face about watching Coltaine die and High Fist Pormqual surrendering, the Aren Guard survived only because Captain [Keneb] found out Mallick Rel was an agent to the enemy Sha’ik
Commander Blistig orders to get Squint cleaned up
Fist Gamet knows Blistig is trying to get himself arrested and sent back to the capital city Unta with his ‘treasonous’ words and omitting important details from his reports
The Malazans needs every soldier they can for the war in Seven Cities, with four new legions incoming from Malaz Island
Blistig looks down upon Gamet as just a house guard and has little confidence in this new 14th Army
Gamet shouts back stating his 23 years of service and involvement in the Wickan Wars, knowing Coltaine since back then, and retiring to become a house guard after taking a lance through the chest.
The Adjunct wants to assemble all her commanders to council that day

Blistig: Commander of the Aren Guard, present when the Chain of Dog refugees came to Aren and opened the doors for them. Stood back helplessly as High Fist Pormqual, puppet to Mallick Rel, refused to rescue Fist Coltaine, instead listening to the nobles’ (Nethpara and Pullyk Alar) poisonous words that Coltaine was a disgrace. Blistig refused Pormqual’s orders to march his soldiers out, then promptly ordered to drop their weapons and be slaughtered, keeping 300 hundred Aren Guard in the city walls and is the reason Aren did not fall to the Whirlwind

Gamet: Briefly seen in Ch. 1 Scene 4, when Ganoes Paran returned home briefly after investigating the Itko Kan in the Quon Tali continent massacre and just before sailing to the Genabackis continent. Tavore had just taken over the House Paran wine merchant business as Felisin was studying.
Squint: The soldier who killed Coltaine with his bow while Coltaine was crucified and being tortured in front of Aren’s walls

Keneb: The captain garrison of Orbal, husband-in-law to Minala. Received help from Bridgeburner Kalam to kill the rebels who destroyed his city. Kalam overheard from the rebels that Aren had a ‘jhistal’ inside and asks Keneb if he knew what that word meant. Kalam escorted Keneb and his family to Aren via Imperial Warren. In Aren, when Keneb heard Duiker call Mallick Rel a ‘jhistal’, that’s when they realized he was a traitor and the Aren Guard remained inside Aren instead of being slaughtered outside.
Strings, aka Fiddler is on a boat entering Aren Bay through the Menykh River
Lt. Ranal is a tall, fair skin and light haired young man, noble-born from Quon that purchased, rather than earned, his position
Lt. Ranal approaches Fiddler at the railings of the ship and demanded he gave a customary salute to his superior officer
Lt. Ranal is concerned why the recruiting officer Fiddler straight through without training, even suggesting to make him a sergeant
Ranal thinks Fiddler is a deserter, but Fiddler retorts deserters wouldn’t re-enlist, and walks away
Koryk, long black-haired half-Seti (native tribe on Quon Tali, like the Wickans), comments that Ranal wanted Fiddler dead and that only new recruits are coming
Fiddler says they’re going to mix recruits with the veterans: Chain of Dog survivors both marines and Wickans, Aren Guard, Red Blades, and Admiral Nok’s fleet
A young female soldier [Smiles] wonders if Tavore is going to be the same as Ranal since she’s noble-born
Fiddler has some confidence, thinking Tavore is Ganoes Paran’s sister, who earned Fiddler’s respect in Darujhistan
Lostara Yil sits down at Dancer’s Tavern, at dusk, answering Pearl’s call he sent via street urchin
She still has some feelings for Pearl but wants to keep to her responsibilities
The Red Blades are few, but more willing to enact vengeance unlike the dispirited Aren Guard
Lostara doesn’t know what to expect from the new Adjunct Tavore, and whether she trusts the Red Blades (since they are native to Seven Cities)
Pearl enters in a cheery mood and pours some wine
Lostara is still pissed she and the Red Blades were arrested for treason by Pormqual
Adjunct Tavore is a mystery to Pearl as well, but is holding a council meeting tonight which Red Blades commander Tene Baralta is invited to
Pearl requested Lostara Yil to be his personal aide
Lostara is angry and doesn’t want to be just an assassin, but Pearl convinces her that it’ll affirm her loyalty to the Malazan Empire
Pearl doesn’t know what their mission will be, but will find out at the meeting
They head to the High Fist’s old palace

Fist Gamet stands at the door of the council chambers, at the table are seated Commander of the Aren Guard Blistig, Commander of the Red Blades Tene Baralta, and Admiral Nok awaiting the first council meeting

Gamet feels self-conscious as he had only been a common soldier before. He feels Tavore is having him manage the entire 14th Army like he managed her household and didn’t earn his position. He has no idea to what Tavore is thinking or what her plans are.
Admiral Nok is the last of the ‘old guard’ along with Dujek Onearm. The only admiral that didn’t ‘drown’ as the Napans like Urko Crust and Cartheron Crust had.

Tavore sent Nok and his 107 ships to Aren when the Whirlwind rumors peaked. They acknowledge that if Pormqual didn’t hold them hostage at Aren Bay, the Chain of Dogs wouldn’t have happened in the first place

Adjunct Tavore Paran enters wearing plain, colourless clothing with her otataral sword at her side, a sign of her office. (Similar to Adjunct Lorn, whose otataral sword is now in Ganoes Paran’s possession)
Tavore sets down six scrolls and rapidly lists off her orders, with little room to respond or discuss which is not the normal imperial style

First scroll: Gamet, Blistig, and Tene Baralta are now Fists of the 8th, 9th, and 10th legions respectively, they can choose their officers. Commander Alardis is to be detached from Admiral Nok and the Aren Guard is now hers to command
Second scroll: The Chain of Dogs survivors are dissolved and dispersed throughout the three legions.
Tavore tells Blistig and Tene Baralta to go to a side chamber to discuss their new command, Admiral Nok is to meet with her in private later that evening.
All other four people in the room are shocked speechless, but follow her orders
Tavore admires the tapestries on the walls and asks Gamet whom the new Fists will choose as their officers
Gamet assumes Tene Baralta will have Red Blades as his officers and Blistig will choose Captain Keneb

Tavore knows Blistig isn’t upset that he was helpless when Coltaine was slaughtered, but because he defied military hierarchy by disobeying a superior commander’s orders. Believes he should be sent to Unta for the consequences.
Blistig doesn’t think Tavore has faith in him.
The Wickan witch Nether, warlock Nil, and 14 year old soldier Temul enter the chamber for the second council meeting
The twins’ clothes were dirty and unkempt. Temul looked enthusiastic and was in immaculate armor with a red face paint for grief
The twins reject Tavore’s position as mages for the Malaz 14th Army and want to go home
Tavore questions Temul
Coltaine had placed Temul in charge of the remaining 41 Wickan youths, and had attached Nil and Nether as their warlocks.
Since Temul’s company has yet to be dissolved, Tavore denies the twins’ request, telling them to find a way to reawaken the spirits that have been silenced within them
Tavore has only 500 inexperienced Seti warriors around Temul’s age incoming, not enough to have a cavalry engagement (mounted horses) thus the 14th Army is mostly ground infantry
Tavore addresses Temul as Captain and assigns them to her personal entourage as bodyguards, the Seti’s will be messengers and scouts.
She asserts this is no longer Coltaine’s war and dismisses them
Tavore asks Gamet how he thinks the other Fists are doing
Gamet thinks Tene Baralta doesn’t want 4000 Malazan recruits himself
Doesn’t know why Admiral Nok didn’t just usurp Pormqual and stop the Aren slaughter. Empress Laseen had no reason to question Admiral Nok’s loyalty
Gamet responds ‘Nor Dujek Onearm’, which Tavore only smiled at

Gamet implies that since Empress Laseen outlawed Dujek and his 2nd Army (which was a secret plot only known to Dujek and Whiskeyjack), it could her fault that Admiral Nok didn’t want to defy the Malazan hierarchy.

Tavore picks up a scroll and walks them to another room. Once Gamet locks the door, Tavore looks at him with anxiety and vulnerability in her eyes for the first time in her life. ‘In this room, the Empress is not present’
Pearl, effeminate and handsome, enters with Lostara Yil
Pearl immediately insults Gamet, and admits that Clawmster Topper is upset with Pearl
Tavore asks Pearl how the Talons are, making him nervous and forcing him to admit they still exist
Tavore shares the Talon found support among the nobles (Paran) and that Baudin had failed her
Baudin’s father had killed numerous Claw agents and took four days to be hunted down
Tavore hands them a scroll, says she’s lost contact with her sister since the Skullcup uprising, and tasks Pearl and Lostara to find Felisin
Gamet flashbacks to the event of the Culling, during the Season of Rot in Unta
Felisin was hiding in the ruined house, Gamet had a dozen guards, Ganoes presumed dead on Genabackis
Rumours spread that Empress Laseen was displeased, that the nobility and ‘purchases of commissions’ was the reason behind imperial incompetent command
The Red Blades, Seven Cities natives incorruptible to noble bribery, had made the arrests
Baudin had been hired under the fake name Kollen to look after Felisin, convinced Gamet to go along with Tavore’s plan to guard her while she is sent to the otataral mines
Lostara Yil refuses to be a part of finding Felisin, not clear how it servers the Malazan Empire
Pearl convinces her Tavore is willing to give up the Talon in exchange for finding Felisin, thus serving the Malazan Empire

They will also have evidence to condemn Tavore, that sending her family to the otataral mines to gain favor and prove her loyalty to the Empire is a lie, which will let Pearl become favored with Clawmaster Topper and Empress Laseen

Talon: The original covert organization under Dancer (Cotillion’s past life). Surly had created her own organization and named it the Claw. Once Surly became Empress, she had ordered for the eradication of any loyalty to the ‘old guard’ including the Talon, thus an internal civil war.
In Deadhouse Gates, Felisin found a talon while rummaging in Baudin’s bag
Adjunct Tavore and Fist Gamet meets with Admiral Nok
Gamet reflects on following Tavore out of curiosity, instead of mysteriously disappearing (a la the Malazan soldier way).
Tavore ordered the arrest of her own parents and her little sister ‘for her career’s sake’
Also thinks about the rumors that Ganoes Paran was disgraced and deserted the army which led to Adjunct Lorn’s death
Admiral Nok and Tavore talk about a missing transport ship in Malaz Harbor, known for its sharks
Nok talks about how the harbor is haunted, sharks always eating Malazans whole with no remains and smells a lot like bullshit. Others that disappeared were Urko, Catheron, and Ameron
Tavore remarks Nok [and Tayschrenn, Dujek Onearm, and Whiskeyjack] are all that’s left from Kellanved’s reign and asks why the ‘missing’ abandoned Empress Laseen
Gamet’s inner thoughts: Tavore has no allies loyal to her, commands in isolation with barriers raised
Nok explains how Kellanved created a family that founded the Malazan Empire

The city-state Unta annexed the Napan Isles to use as a staging point to invade Kartool Island, as well as had a partnership with Mock, the pirate-king of Malaz Island [and Tattersail’s lover at the time]
Nok, his wife Hawl, and Ameron were on a pirate ship around the Napan Isles and were arrested by Mock when they sailed into Malaz Harbor
They trio escaped, and were found by Dujek who brought them to Kellanved and Dancer
Kellanved and Dancer found Deadhouse (the Azath house in Malaz City) and were given gifts of longevity, immunity to most diseases, and an unassailable base of operations
Kellanved then hired several others to complete his family that conquered the Malaz Island
Refugee Napans: Cartheron Crust and Urko Crust, captains of the Napan fleet, Surly of a royal line
Toc Elder, Whiskeyjack
Dassem Ultor (Dal Honese like Kellanved)
Tayschrenn (renegade High Septarch of D’rek, Worm of Autumn and Queen of Disease)
Hawl died in the attempt
The Napans wanted to crush the Untan hegemony and were using Kellanved (the first fissure in the family)
Surly’s assassination of Kellanved and Dancer destroyed Kellanved’s family completely
Joshua
Butler
Tavore notices it was only Napans that deserted Surly/Laseen despite her being a Napan royal
Cartheron, Urko, and Ameron were against the assassination, Surly didn’t include them in her plans, they felt shame and they abandoned her
Gamet accidentally asks about the Talons, Nok said he only knows they went missing when Dancer died
Tavore adjourns her last meeting and goes to find T’Amber
In the stables, Fiddlers/Strings look at Koryk tie fetishes to his body and thinks about Seti culture
The Seti tribe fought Quon and Li Heng city-states for centuries, but have become pacified for the past 60 years with three generations
Eventually the majority of the native tribes ended up becoming mixed with peculiar results. The Seti tribe originally did not know how to ride horses, and know they’re known as horse warriors
Koryk seems to have a culture clash, a Malazan marine trying to emulate his ancestral traditions
Fiddler explains the current hierarchy to the four recruits and makes one of them corporal
Corporal Tarr, a pale man with stolid features, from Li Heng. Named because he can stand firm with a shield against a battering ram. Doesn’t talk much.
Smiles, female recruit, never smiles
Bottle, mage. Plain young man wearing leather and holds no weapons
Braven Tooth was their drill sergeant, the person responsible for giving new names to almost all Malazan soldiers
Braven Tooth got his name when he left a tooth in Fiddler’s shoulder in a bar brawl
Fiddler hears complaining outside, Sergeant Gesler of the 5th Squad introduces himself
Fiddler recognizes Gesler, Stormy, and Truth as ‘old guard’, notices their tempered bronze skin
Stormy jokes that they should’ve gotten a new name like ‘Strings’
The squads form up in the abandoned courtyard
Fiddler and Gesler joke about deranking as ‘old guard’, along with Whiskeyjack who got outlawed
Fiddler reveals who he is to Gesler and they shake hands, agreeing to swap stories
Apart of the ‘Old Guard’ that served during Kellanved’s reign. Served as coastal guard near Hissar during Deadhouse Gates. Followers of Fener, the Boar of War.

When Hissar was attacked by the Whirlwind Rebellion, they joined imperial historian Duiker and mage Kulp to flee on the ship, the Ripath, and sail to the otataral mines to rescue exiled historian Heboric.
On the otataral coast, they found Felisin, Heboric, and Baudin who just escaped the Skullcup mines after the uprising. An unnamed insane mage dragged them to the Nascent
The group of eight explore the Nascent and find the Silanda, find the remains of the Tiste Edur Karsa Orlong slaughtered during his time spent in the Nascent
Six Logros T’lan Imass appear, they are pursuing renegade kin (The Seven Faces in the Rock)
When Karsa harpooned the tiste edur mage, he died midcast so his warren stayed open and became a wound
Legana Breed gives Stormy his flint sword, and sacrifices himself to close the warren wound
Kulp used his Meanas (illusion) warren to find an undead dragon, ‘The Unwelcome’, and drags the Silanda in its wake to escape
The dragon takes the ship through the Meanas warren, and then the Tellann warren of fire which made Gesler, Stormy, and Truth ascend, tempering their skin to bronze
The Silanda lands with only the coastal guard trio near Vathar Crossing and intersect with Coltaine’s Chain of Dogs
Captain Lull promotes them, Gesler teases that he’ll punch him and pull Coltaine’s thong. Coltaine laughs and punches his metal faces, breaking his own hand
The trio take all the wounded from the Chain of Dogs on the Silanda and sail to Aren
After the slaughter outside Aren, the old guard trio look for Duiker’s body and rescue the dogs Roach and Bent
Crokus, Apsalar, and her father Rellock return to their home on the fishing coast of Itko Kan
Rellock passes away in his sleep, Apsalar grieved beside him
Crokus believes he saw footprints of Hood or his servant that collect Rellock’s soul
Feels that Apsalar is darker and more mysterious after Cotillion’s possession, may be approaching ascendancy
Crokus ponders about ascendancy, believing it to be surrendering mortality and its first love, life
He likes her and wants to follow her, even if he’s scared of her
Crokus saw that people were slowly repopulating the area
Believes in his journey, he lost the fear of dying. He goes outside to practice his knife handling skills
He look at their own boat on the shore and remembers Shadowthrone sending them to an alleyway in Kan, where a bookmaker gave them a boat in exchange for killing the people extorting him
A bystander saw Crokus and ran away in fright
Crokus resolved to separate his identity from the innocent thief he was before and named himself ‘Cutter of the Knives’, to walk at Apsalar’s side similar to Kellanved and Dancer
Apsalar asks what does Crokus want to do next
A simple fishergirl was possessed by Cotillion and Rigga the Seer, a wax witch, before the slaughter of Itko Kan
Rigga the Seer was grieving her family lost in war, foresaw Apsalar’s possession and thus wanted to protect her
Shadowthrone and Cotillion wanted revenge for their deaths, planned to use her for the Empire’s downfall
She enlisted under the name Sorry and was attached to the Bridgeburners
In Darujhistan, the mischievous god Oponn gifted Crokus Younghand a coin which made him a target by several people, including Sorry, who did not want Oponn disrupting any of their plans
Right before attacking Crokus, Anomander Rake threatened Shadowthrone with Dragnipur to stop his schemes in Darujhistan and thus ended Sorry’s possession
Rigga the Seer’s protection kept Sorry’s mind from shattering
Crokus Younghand takes Sorry back to the city and gives her the name Apsalar, after the Lady of Thieves
Crokus was swept up in the events in the Malazan conflicts against Darujhistan.
His uncle Mammot was possessed by the Jaghut Tyrant Raest and was killed
Tasked by Anomander Rake to protect Alchemist Baruk, knocked the assassin Vorcan unconscious with two bricks which saved Baruk’s life
Once the conflict was over, the Bridgeburners (then outlawed) had found Sorry. Realizing she is no longer possessed and feeling pity for her, Kalam and Fiddler decide to take her home to Itko Kan.
Crokus decides to tag along
Fiddler and Kalam found an opportunity to take revenge against Empress Laseen for their annihilation at the Siege of Pale and their outlawry.

Decided to detour to Seven Cities. Kalam would initiate the Whirlwind Rebellion while Fiddler takes Crokus and Apsalar to find the Tremorlor, an Azath House, somewhere on the continent that connects to the Deadhouse, an Azath House in Malaz City.
As a backup plan, they wanted to use Apsalar’s skills gained by Cotillion to have her assassinate Laseen
Fiddler, Crokus, and Apsalar are attacked by soletaken and d’ivers, but are saved by Icarium and Mappo Runt
They are very friendly and take them to Tesem Temple, a temple of Shadow inhabited by Iskaral Pust
Most likely from Shadowthrone and Cotillion’s schemes, Apsalar’s father Rellock had been sent to Iskaral Pust as his servant.

Iskaral made a deal with Rellock, to spare his and Apsalar’s lives and restore his missing arm, in exchange for planting false trails leading the soletaken and d’ivers away from the Path of Hands to be trapped by the Azath House, Tremorlor
Iskaral tried to make Apsalar become Sha’ik Reborn and trap Icarium in Tremorlor, which both failed
The group fought their way to Tremorlor, only Crokus, Apsalar, Rellock, and Fiddler were transported to the Deadhouse in Malaz City
They reunite with Kalam, who had spoken to Empress Laseen and gave up his plan to kill her
Apsalar requests Shadowthrone to take her, her father, and Crokus back to her home in Itko Kan and sever all ties between them and the gods
Kalam got kicked out of the house by Minala and so he’s just wandering on horseback
On a grassy hill, are mortared pillars where every 12th pillar was chained to a monstrous arm that had talons and two thumbs, the creatures themselves lost to insanity
Kalam ponders on his life, he likes his relationship with Minala who was teaching the 1,300 children survival and weapon handling skills, grooming an army for Shadowthrone. Along with Apt.
Cotillion approaches with the Hounds, Rood and Blind
Cotillion has something for him to do, and Kalam basically says yes because he’s bored and has nothing else to do  ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
Night time, Crokus makes a campfire and tea on the beach as Apsalar walks off by herself
Cotillion approaches, Crokus is very cheeky with his ‘patron god’. Character progression.
Rejects Cotillions offer to have his weapons blessed with magic
