(Note: It’s probably a domestic demon, Erikson is hilarious that way)
While thinking about how to phrase his command to quietly capture Irriz, the Azalan receives via telepathy
The Azalan demon lifts his hind leg and pisses in the latrine pit with its two dicks, Kalam runs out of the tent and gags. The urine steams and crackles from within
A moment later the Azalan demon exits the tent and go finds Irriz
Walking away towards the rope to the Ashok, his tent bursts into flames which alerts the camp
Halfway up the cliff, the Azalan demon climbs up the cliff with Irriz
The cliff and balcony above Kalam crack underneath the Azalan’s weight, shadows emanate from the demon like arms trying to hold the cliff together
Kalam rushes to the balcony and is pulled into a corridor by an Ashok Regiment squad mage, Ebron
The Azalan hops into the corridor and the balcony collapses
Sgt. Cord, squad mage Ebron, Bell, Cpl. Shard, and Sinn greet Kalam
Kalam reveals who he is and admits the Bridgeburner outlawry was a feint
Cpt. Kindly and Lt. Pores are presumed dead, climbed down a well to explore and was swept away in the underground river
As his superior, Sgt. Cord welcomes Cpl. Kalam to the 51-member, 2nd Company of the Ashok Regiment
The soldiers want the Azalan gone or leashed, Kalam dares them to control a domestic demon that wiped out 500 rebel warriors in less than a minute
Kalam is willing up follow their lead, but only if it’s reasonable to him and to take it up with Whiskeyjack is they have a problem
(Note: Kalam doesn’t know yet about the events of Memories of Ice and that Whiskeyjack’s dead)
Ebron thinks Kalam is Laseen’s Claw again
Kalam mutters that this trip is going to be rough
Sinn dances around
Crokus and Apsalar have reached Drift Avalii with a storm approaching
(Note: We don’t know why Cotillion sent them here yet)
Looks like a flat island of just cedars, firs, and redwoods
Crokus had a hard time prodding Apsalar to speak in days, getting frustrated at times
Apsalar grows quiet, still possessing Cotillion’s memories and knowledge, and anger that Crokus has become Cotillion’s minion, especially when changing his name to Cutter
Crokus is trying to be closer to Apsalar but it makes her want to push him away even more
Crokus never needed to be a thief and was well off, but was proud in his skills as a thief. Thought the same enthusiasm was shared in Apsalar’s skill in assassination.
‘Apsalar was trying to tell him that competence was not justification. That necessity demanded its own path and there was no virtue to be found at its heart’
‘He’d found himself at subtle war with her, the weapons those of silence and veiled expressions’
From Dancer’s memories, Anomander Rake left Tiste Andii people on the island and never came back for them
The coast was sandstone, vortices of water being pulled under and pushed out
Crokus jumps onto a stone ledge while holding a rope, the thin shelf collapsed under his feet and the boat ran him over and capsized
Crokus gets pulled underneath the island by the water currents into a pitch dark pocket cave with air
Crokus swam blindly in the dark pocket until he found a ledge to hold onto, too weak to get out
Darist pulls him up. A tall old man with ebony skin, long white hair and beard, and glowing amber eyes the only source of light in the cave. Heat radiated from the man
Darist waved his hand, a stone wall opened to reveal a set of stairs. He warns they should leave before something wakes up
Up the stairs ran a corridor with pillars of cedar trunks
Crokus lies and says Baruk sent him to investigate the Tiste Edur threat that assails the unoccupied Throne of Shadow
Darist and the Tiste Andii don’t care about the world outside (which everyone thinks is why they’re in this trouble)
Darist thinks Crokus might’ve been sent by Rake. Upset that if Rake isn’t happy with how they’re doing their job, he should come tell them himself.
It appears Rake gave up his claim to Tiste Andii blood when he took on Draconian blood
Crokus says he only say Rake once, fighting the Galayn demon in Darujhistan, no position to talk to him
Cotillion only planned to have Crokus sneak onto the island unseen and see if the Tiste Edur found it
Felt insignificant being a god’s pawn, and come between Rake and the Tiste Andii’s conflict
Thought Cutter’s persona would give him freedom, but it’s the opposite
Memories of Ice
The Throne of Shadow has summoned Ganoes Paran, the Master of the Deck, and told Paran that the Tiste Edur’s souls were corrupted and poisoned.
The throne says Anomander Rake’s children are gone, sacrificing their own lives to lead the Tiste Edur away from the throne and are begging for Rake’s help
Crokus is worried about Apsalar and wants to wait, but Darist only senses the presence of Tiste Edur and is confident his friend is dead
‘Death is not an unkind fate. If she was your friend, you will miss her company, and that is the true source of your grief - your sorrow is for yourself’
‘Darist, forgive me. You may be old, but you are also a damned fool. And I begin to understand why Rake left you here then forgot about you. Now, kindly shut up’
Darist blankly says they’ve already lost. He is the last one standing.
Two spirits are trapped in the big dog statues in front of Onrack and Trull Sengar
The clouds dissipated revealing three moons and two suns
T’lan Imass bonecasters creating an icon can capture the essence of a god or spirit and seal it away
Onrack misunderstands Trull’s interpretation, thinks he’s talking about the origin of the Tiste Edur
Trull ponders if Mother Dark created the Tiste Edur by separating the shadow from the Tiste Andii
The statues do not have shadows. Like the Tiste Andii who had their shadows ‘separated’ by Mother Dark, perhaps Hounds of Darkness exist as well
The Logros had come to the First Empire to deal with the chaos of the Soletaken and D’ivers
Once the Beast Ritual was unleashed, the human founder Dessimbelackis disappeared and was rumored to have become a D’ivers of seven beasts
As a Tiste Edur, Trull doesn’t think his people created the statues and they don’t worship the Hounds of Shadow. They are ‘untethered’
The Tiste Edur seek the Throne of Shadow and to reunite the fragments of Kurald Emurlahn
Trull believes an outsider has corrupted the Tiste Edur and is manipulating them
Trull thinks Onrack can empathize with seeing their own people fall apart, become corrupt, and struggle endlessly against time
Onrack thinks the Tiste Edur people with be either discarded or annihilated after their purpose is fulfilled
‘There is the unpleasant ring of truth to your words, Onrack’
‘I am generally unpleasant, Trull Sengar’

cards.h: *** First Empire Ruins in Deadhouse Gates

i.html: Ch. 14 Scene 1
When Felisin, Heboric, and Kulp escaped the Nascent realm they traveled for three days in the Whirlwind and found a cave that led to the ruins of an ancient First Empire city
The First Empire attempted to give the Path of the Soletaken to their young to achieve an alternative path to Ascendancy

All around them were petrified humans, in various stages of veering and shapeshifting, butchered by the T’lan Imass of the past [Now we know this was done by the Logros and Onrack] which Heboric dubs “immortal custodians”
Felisin drank water that makes her feel “mended”
A grand temple had friezes that depicted the Holds, Elder versions of the Deck of Dragons
Through the temple they were able to escape back into the holy desert Raraku
Trull tries to probe what Onrack knows of the statues, to Onrack’s displeasure
Onrack thinks two Hounds were killed and ended up here. He thinks it’d be fun to kill a Hound himself
Onrack swung his obsidian sword against the statue, which cracked them both and freed the Hounds of Shadow within
The Hounds’ shoulder was as tall as Trull. The suns and moons casted several shadows below them.
The Hounds dodges Onrack’s sword and bites on him, shaking him tearing Onrack’s left arm off
The Hound tossed Onrack in the air to the other Hound which did the same
One final tossed in the air and Onrackfell into a pile of bones. The Hounds’ attacks were violent enough that it actually sundered Onrack’s Vow and cut him off from the rest of the T’lan Imass.
Onrack could no longer turn his body to dust
The Hounds simply walk away, Trull approaches and says they must be Hounds of Darkness
‘So much for gratitude’
Trull Sengar sets Onrack at the edge of the city wall

Onrack says if his kin were there to carry out the ‘necessary rites’, they would cut off his head to place at a comfortable spot, chop up and scatter his body, and take his weapon back to his birthplace
Onrack can no longer sense the ‘gates’ in the city to leave, but Trull is not discouraged
Like Trull, Onrack has been shorn from his people

Trull and Onrack explored the city. It’s architecture was simple, smoothed, and composed to fired brick. It was covered with layers of wet silt. The streets led to a city square with pedestals that used to hold statues
The sun above was blue, and the moon was magenta
At the end of the city square was a bridge over a river covered with silt, with masses of trash spilling onto the path
Among the trash was a box, which Onrack recognized as being full of Moranth munitions belonging to the Malazan Empire ‘of his birth realm’
[Note: These are Moranth Munitions that Torvald Nom possessed earlier and abandoned when they escaped. Eventually they floated through the breach to here]
Walking forward, they found an arch that was pulsating scalding heat and ridges of clay hardened to rock at its mouth
Onrack threw one of the clay sphere munitions at the gate which detonated. It was enough to ‘shatter the pattern’ which ‘sorcery depends on’
White and gold fires raged and formed into a swirling golden wall; destroying the ward and reactivating the gate
Onrack senses something coming from the gate and Trull runs back over the bridge
Unable to run himself, Onrack intends to buy time for his friend to flee
Four riders on white horses and rust-coloured manes entered
Ornate enamel armor, slitted visors with cheek guards, gauntlets holding curved ivory scimitars
The riders were tall, pale skinned, with long silver hair
Onrack attacked as the bridge was narrow for only two horses at a time
Onrack shattered one of their enamel armor as two of them shattered his clavicle and right side of his face and rode past
Onrack came to his knees and held up his obsidian sword to guard himself, the other two riders swung at him as they rode past
The rider took off his helm, his features strikingly similar to Trull Sengar’s people but with pale skin
The rider, Enias, asks if Onrack can speak the ‘Language of Purity’, gets offended by Onrack, names him a servant of Death, and says prepare to die
The other rider that Onrack injured, Seneschal Jorrude, tells him to wait. The portal hasn’t been used in millenia and they’re not in their world anymore
Onrack recognizes them as Tiste

Enias responds the Tiste Liosan are the purest. The Tiste Andii are their tained vermin cousins, imperfect and ‘bereft of Father Light’s purifying blood’ that deserve death. The Tiste Edur are tolerated because they have part of Light in them.
The rider took off his helm, his features strikingly similar to Trull Sengar’s people but with pale skin
The rider, Enias, asks if Onrack can speak the ‘Language of Purity’, gets offended by Onrack who says it’s no purer than any other, names him a servant of Death, and says prepare to die
The other rider that Onrack injured, Seneschal Jorrude, tells him to wait. The portal hasn’t been used in millenia and the riders not in their world anymore
Onrack recognizes them as Tiste

Enias responds the Tiste Liosan are the purest. The Tiste Andii are their tained vermin cousins, imperfect and ‘bereft of Father Light’s purifying blood’ that deserve death. The Tiste Edur are tolerated because they have part of Light in them.
Onrack says the T’lan Imass have a habit of proclaiming eternal war against arrogant creatures and that the Tiste Liosan might be fun to hunt for awhile
Enias is shocked, while Malachar says he is the poison that will try to lead them astray from the righteous path
Onrack gets tired of them, sheathes his weapon, and starts walking away
The Liosan threaten him and they all unsheathe their weapon again (This a comedy I tell you, a comedy)
Trull appears with the box of Moranth munitions with a mischievous smile
Four T’lan Imass appeared around him via dust
Onrack greets them, unable to telepathically, and recognizes bonecaster Monok Ochem and clan leader Ibra Gholan
Bonecaster Monok Ochem says Onrack has failed the ritual and will be destroyed
The Tiste Liosan agree to ‘hand over’ their prisoner and invites Trull to be their Edur servant
Trull says they can rotate serving each other and learn humility (basically fuck off)
The Liosan thought they could simply leave, but the Gates are wounded

Monok Ochem knows the Liosan has isolated themselves that they know nothing about the outside world. Their lord Osric, Son of Father Light, has not been with the Liosan because he is lost and hasn’t been home
Even the Liosan didn’t know what happened to Osric
To get home, Monok Ochem suggests they perform a ritual weaving Tellann, Liosan’s warren, and Trull’s blood as a Tiste Edur
Karsa Orlong thinks about his people and misses Bairoth Gild, wishes he was still alive to guide him
He finished carving the Seven Faces of the Teblor gods, but felt something was missing
Feels that Raraku is in a constant state of waiting for rebirth
Snakes continue to slither harmlessly at his feet
Leoman came to visit and Karsa explains who the carvings are
Sha’ik’s council are excited about ‘distant Malazan defeats’ and Felisin has permitted Mathok to march beyond the Whirlwind barrier to harass the incoming Malazan army
Felisin being a Malazan herself is a secret known only to Karsa, Leoman, and Heboric
After years of learning, Karsa realizes the Malazans are no crueler as any other culture
The war is about Malazan justice vs. Seven Cities freedom to terrorize their own people
Leoman has no loyalties, because humans are more destructive than compassionate. The world is better off when humans eradicate themselves
Karsa looks at the carvings, the way the light shines on them makes them look almost human
Sha’ik’s council examines the new House of Chains cards within the Deck of Dragons that were delivered alongside the news of distant Malazan defeats on Genabackis
Reaver, Consort, the Unbound. Each was painted with flaws

Munug had delivered the painted cards to the Crippled God at the beginning of Memories of Ice. He wanted to cure the painful tumors in his legs, and the Crippled God ‘cured him’ by paralyzing him from the waist down
Felisin makes Bidithal pull out the Master of the Deck card and wants Heboric to try to examine it
The man’s face is obscured, standing on a stone bridge surrounded by soldiers with a backdrop of flames behind them. The soldiers stand on helmeted, non-human skulls and bones
Arms held out, feet together as if forming a point
Wears tight, black silks. A wrought iron chain from his left shoulder to his right hip. Four wooden discs like epaulets on his shoulders
Heboric’s interpretation: ‘He is one sword, above all, and it uts cold. That sword is as this man’s own nature. He will cleave his own path. None shall lead him’
Heboric can see his face in his mind, and recognizes him as Felisin’s brother
He says to have faith in the Master of the Deck against the House of Chains
Fel Younger helps Heboric leave the council chamber and Heboric ponders on the war

Korbolo Dom is training the Whirlwind army with Malazan training, the Malazan Army will face an enemy with equal training for the first time (their training was the most elite in the world at this point)
The Whirlwind has several high mages, while Tavore’s 14th Army has no high mages
But the Malazans do have Moranth munitions
Thinks the Wickan warlock twins are broken and can’t cast anymore
Fel Younger tells Heboric that he needs to leave and retrace his steps. An entire island of otataral was made to contain the power of the giant statue
The otataral is fading in Heboric’s ghost hands, the jade trapped inside him might be released
Heboric is angry because the Whirlwind’s war  has been stolen and is just a stage for a Malazan family to quarrel with each other
Fel Younger says she will go on this journey with him, and find a warrior as well
Leoman tells Karsa of Jhag horses in the Jhag Odhan that might be big enough for Karsa
There are cliffs at the edge of Raraku that used to be the shoreline when the desert was an ancient sea
Travel westward to Lato Revae, follow the Thalas Mountains, follow the Ugarat River to Y’Ghatan, then travel southwest two more weeks to reach the Jhag Odhan
Leoman says the T’lan Imass had slaughtered all of the Jaghut, Karsa recognizes the T’lan Imass in Teblor history
Note: The T’lan Imass had warred with the Forkrul Assail and imprisoned Calm beneath that boulder. The bones of Bone Pass were T’lan Imass
Karsa asks about Fel Younger, Leoman says Heboric is ware of Bidithal
Leoman and his people will scout ahead for the incoming Malazan army past the Whirlwind barrier, Karsa will come find him if he doesn’t return by the end of his horse journey
Leoman leaves to inform Felisin about his plan, and mentions she’s focused on the House of Chains
Karsa hates and is haunted by chains, ‘This new House - is it mine?’
The air becomes cold, the snakes flee. Karsa’s mind is full of howling winds, souls moaning, chains rattling and snapping. The Seven Faces awaken
The Faces are offended by Karsa’s carvings of Bairoth and Delum and commands to destroy them
Karsa warns them that he can destroy the Faces, he is no longer the gullible Teblor, and stood strong against the Faces’ outburst of anger
The Faces wants him to journey westward, away from the ‘petty spirit that spits sand’, and free them
‘Because, at last, I am my father’s son’
The Faces disappeared
Karsa turns his attention to his two friends, the true people he sanctified the forest for

‘My loyalty was misplaced. I served only glory. Words, my friends. And words can wear false nobility. Disgusting brutal truths. The words of the past, that so clothed the Teblor in a hero’s garb - this is what I served. While the true glory was before me. Beside me. You, Delum Thord. And you, Bairoth Gild.’
Delum and Bairoth’s souls awaken. ‘Lead us, Warleader’
‘Delum Thord. Bairoth Gild. It is I who failed you. I would be your warleader once more, if you would os permit me’
‘Karsa fell to his knees. Grief, finally unleashed. At an end, his time of solitude. His penance was done. The journey to begin again. Dear Urugal, you shall witness. Oh, how you shall witness.
Heboric rebuilds his hearthfire too big and ponders on death as L’oric enters
L’oric wants to exchange information about the jade hand for what Heboric knows about the the Master of the Deck
He brews hen’bara tea, seeing that Heboric looks exhausted
L’oric mentions that scholars have linked Rashan (human/dark), Thyr (human/light), and Meanas (human/shadow) as a triumvirate and link it to their Elder counterparts
Anomander Rake had asserted a claim on the Throne of Shadow by having Tiste Andii (Darist) guard it against the Tiste Edur
L’oric ponders on human history and how it’s defined by the rise and fall of tyrants. To the Tiste people, the worst tyrants never go away and are eternal
Heboric laughs, saying that Dark, Light, and Shadow are like mother, father, and child. But with humans involving themselves, it’s like the in-laws and grandchildren are joining in their mess
L’oric froze, initially warning that Tiste are a threat to humans but Heboric made him realized the Tiste are the ones that should be scared
L’oric knows that Heboric is Malazan that escaped from the otataral mines. Heboric is worried about spies
L’oric knows of the sorceries flying in the air scrying on rivals and made preparations to make both L’oric and Heboric appear resting in their own beds
Heboric relents that the Master of the Deck is related to the Bridgeburners killed by the Pannion Domin
L’oric asks if Heboric has heard of Spiritwalker Kimloc who gave [Fiddler] a Tanno song
Also remarks that Tanno sorcery is “elliptical”, the Bridgeburners were born in the Raraku desert, and one of them needs to return here for the song to sanctify the company
L’oric reveals the first jade giant was found in the otataral mines. Three veins were found and sealed away.
The giants are intruders from another realm. Each arrival anticipated, thus chained in otataral

Heboric recall a female scholar that suggested otataral was created when sorcery had drained or annihilated all energy around it - like slag with the ore burned out (slag being the melted rock to harvest the raw ore)
A power that gods do not have, but two events might fit the criteria: The Ritual of Tellann and the calling down of the Crippled God
L’oric then told Heboric something offscreen as we pan away
‘Together, there at the ends of [Heboric’s] wrists, they became the weight of the world’
At the beginning of Deadhouse Gates, Fiddler was in Ehrlitan where Red Blades were slaughtering those they accused of being allies to the cult of Dryjhna
Fiddler sees a pimp/child trafficker and buys two girls from them to rescue them. The girls’ guards find Fiddler and take them to the girls’ grandfather’s home, Kimloc

Kimloc, a Tanno Spiritwalker, is grateful and offers a Tanno song where all he needs is to touch Fiddler and learn his history, Fiddler rejects (but he touches his shoulder anyways without Fiddler noticing)
Also gives Fiddler a conch shell with power invested in it
In Tremorlor, Fiddler accidentally throws the conch shell instead of a Moranth munition which obliterated shapeshifters all around them and gave him a vision of Raraku still as an ocean
Kalam knew who Kimloc is, and would kill Kimloc if he could. Some feud that’s never known to readers
Leoman sees Karsa off as he departs for his journey to the Jhag Odhan to find a Jhag horse
‘Tell me, what would your kin say to you in parting?’
‘May you slay a thousand children’
Leoman blanched. ‘Journey well, Toblakai’
Flanked by the spirits of Bairoth Gild and Delum Thord, Karsa Orlong sets off
‘If there must be ghosts, it was better to lead them than to be chased by them’
Korbolo Dom and Kamist Reloe are monitoring Karsa’s departure
Leoman and Heboric are their remaining obstacles between them and Felisin Paran
Their plan is to have Febryl kill Felisin
→ Tavore kill Febyrl
→ the Dogslayers to defeat Tavore
→ Korbolo Dom and Kamist Reloe will crush the rebellion became seen as heroes to Empress Laseen
Mallick Rel continues southward to complete his role in the scheme
Korbolo Dom kicks Kamist Reloe out so he can spend alone time with Fayelle
Korbolo Dom’s ultimate goal is to somehow destroy magic and obliterate every other race from the world under his rule
Korbolo Dom seems very happy that Whiskeyjack is dead
Adjunct Tavore leads the Malaz 14th Army out of Aren towards the Holy Desert Raraku
The army passes the hill where Coltaine died, swarmed with ants
Seven Cities tribes made pilgrimage and left tributes to Coltaine’s shrine, known as the Fall
Kherahn Dhobri: ‘Red-stained braids, woven in chains, draped across the summit and coil around the twin stumps of the cross that had once stood there’
Khundryl Burned Tears: ‘Dog skulls with runes’
Bhilard: Banners of a broken Wickan long knife
Semk: Crow feathers and beads at their stems
Aren Way is lined all the way with tributes like this, Tavore will have to travel all the way to Raraku in the shadow of Coltaine
The Crow Clan reject Temul as their commander
Tene Baralta asks Gamet what Tavore has done to earn such loyalty and be equal to Coltaine
‘Gods, what answer to make to that? Damn you, Tene, can you not see the truth before you? She has done . . . nothing. I beg you. Leave an old man to his faith.’
Sgt. Fiddler and Sgt. Gesler argue about the point of having faith
Gesler says his last commander was Korbolo Dom who used to worship Whiskeyjack and thought he had the potential to become emperor of the Malazan Empire, felt betrayed that he did not
Fiddler thinks once the armies from Genabackis land on Seven Cities, Korbolo Dom can face Whiskeyjack himself (Note: They don’t know of Whiskeyjack’s death yet)
The Malaz 14th Army were flying their own banner

‘A grimy, thin-limbed figure holding a bone aloft, the details in dun colours that were barely visible on a yellow ochre field, the border a woven braid of imperial magenta and dark gray. A defiant figure standing before a sandstorm’
Fiddler ponders on how it seems to reflect Tavore and Sha’ik, not Tavore and Coltaine whose path they’re retreading
Fiddler hears a [Tanno] song faintly in his head and ponders on returning to Raraku
The first time made him ‘mysteriously renewed’ as he doesn’t look or feel as old as he should be
Raraku stole something of the Bridgeburner’s mortality and replaced it with something else
Sgt. Fiddler assessed the army, will take a few days before journeying on foot in full gear was second nature. Minor healers exhausted fending off heat exposure and dehydration
Koryk appeared to have the ‘mailed fist that every squad needed’
Cpl. Tarr was stubborn
Smiles was eerie and reminded Fiddler of Sorry. Made a beached porpoise reference placing her origin on some coastside
Squad Mage Bottle was shy for a mage
Sapper Cuttle was someone Fiddler could trust, reminded him of Hedge
Sgt. Gesler points out the tree that Duiker was tied to and disappeared the day after
Noted that Emperor [Kellanved] saw something in Duiker as a soldier and decided he should be educated as imperial historian as well as earning Coltaine’s trust to lead the refugees
Gesler remembered Coltain punching his face, as hard as Urko Crust, and willing to give Adjunct Tavore a chance
The horn sounded the army to take a break
Sgt. Fiddler notes Sgt. Gesler and Sgt. Borduke’s squad mages were almost identical. The overweight mage Balgrid looked pale and their squad healer Lutes came to him
Gesler noted that Balgrid, his squad mage Tavod Pond, and Bottle all used Meanas (human/dark), Fiddler figured they could come together and make a big illusion
Lt. Ranal comes to see if they have any mages
Gesler was going to deny but was cut off by Fiddler that said they did, wants to give Lt. Ranal a chance and had trust in Captain Keneb
First day of the journey was done and Fist Gamet walks to Adjunct Tavore’s command tent guarded by Temul’s Wickans
Gamet pities Temul who was losing his control over the Crow Clan
Tavore places her otataral sword in a stone box and sealed the lid with wax
Tavore says they’re awaiting news and wants glasses of wine
Gamet saw concern in her face and gets anxious
‘A portal flowered, spreading outward like liquid staining a sheet of gauze, murky grey, sighing out a breath of stale, dead air’
Clawmaster Topper appears saying he got drunk with Tayschrenn and he has news of ‘terrible losses’
Squad Mage Bottle lay in the grass ignoring Strings [Fiddler] calling for him
His grandmother told him to ignore the warrens to seek deep, older magic in the roots and tendrils - the links between all creatures - and to ride them
Bottle had a private fascination with warrens, and Meanas (human/dark)
Through his sorcery, Bottle eavesdrops on Tavore’s conversation with Topper
Sgt. Fiddler, Gesler, and Borduke gather their squad mages Balgrid and Tavos Pond who can’t find or sense Bottle. They think he deserted
Bottle comes in and says a portal opened in Tavore’s tent
For the first time they find out the Bridgeburners and Whiskeyjack are dead
Fiddler’s mind goes numb, takes a few steps away, and collapses on the grass
Hearing crying, Fiddler follows the sound and finds Temul frustrated that the Crow Clan is rejecting his command
Fiddler tells Temul of one of his commanders in the same position as Temul that ended up with a knife in his back (Note: Captain Paran) which makes Temul laugh
Fiddler assures Temul that Tavore also faces the same challenge and wants to support Temul
Fiddler advises him to have the inexperienced Seti steal the horses from the Crown Clan and have them walk for a day or several
Temul has more respect for Duiker than Coltaine, because Coltaine performed the duty given to him but Duiker went above and beyond as just a historian
Temul tells Fiddler about Coltaine before reborn when the crows collected his soul and placed it in an empty vessel of an infant
Also the ‘saving stone’ meant for Coltaine that Duiker wore, and potentially activated explaining his disappearance
Duiker gave Temul the responsibility of the refugees
Temul keeps Duiker’s horse because he believes he’ll return
While on the Chain of Dogs, the Trygalle Trade Guild were hired by Dujek Onearm and the cabal council of Darujhistan to deliver life-saving supplies to Coltaine and the refugees

Wondering how an outlaw could pull rank, Dujek told them ‘Never underestimate the Empress’ and ‘The Empress cannot lose such leaders such as Coltaine of the Crow Clan’, at this point Coltaine and Duiker knew the outlawry was a feint
Quick Ben also gave the Trygalle Trade Guild a ‘small oblong bottle of smoky gray glass on a silver chain’ to deliver to Coltaine, who rejected it and tossed it to Duiker
When Duiker was captured outside, Mallick Rel slapped Duiker to the ground and the bottle smashed against his chest
When Squint headshotted Coltaine, his soul rose to be collected by the crows who also retrieved his body
In the Deadhouse Gates epilogue, a pregnant woman who thought her baby was dead was about to drink something that would abort the baby, but the murder of crows come and the baby moves again
Baruk sent two familiars, Irp and Rudd, to retrieve the glass shards and Duiker’s body and take them back to Darujhistan
In the Memories of Ice epilogue, Duiker is in K’rul’s Tavern and tells the ‘dead’ Bridgeburners the story of Coltaine and the Chain of Dogs
Clawmaster Topper brought news that the outlawry of the Bridgeburners was a feint
All the Bridgeburners died and were witnessed being interred in Moon’s Spawn
There was no dishonour to House Paran, Ganoes wasn’t a renegade or responsible for Adjunct Lorn’s death
‘The sacrifice of young Felisin might have, in the end, proved . . . unnecessary’

, and springs backwards away from them

. Crokus throws a second knife caught against a sealskin shield

But then he realized his psyche would never berate him this much (lmao)
The wolves surround Karsa, and to his surprise, harmlessly sprint and form a half circle
The D’ivers, Ryllandaras, speaks in his mind that he are impressed in his endurance and traveling for four days and three nights, and no longer wish to hurt him
He warns that many deadly powers vie for Karsa’s soul
Also warns that Karsa is on someone’s trail, if he ever meets them the world would regret it
Karsa knows it’s a duo side-by-side with one person taller
Ryllandaras leaves
Karsa, to Bairoth’s dismay, decides to meet the duo anyways
Ryllandaras, brother of Treach, approached Mappo and Icarium at the beginning of Deadhouse Gates and backed tf up when he realized who they were.
Was currently hunting Apt, the aptorian demon at the time and even attacked Kalam when he was with the demon
Ryllandars, Treach, and Messremb were the only survivors of the First Empire after the T’lan Imass had slaughtered them for performing the Beast Ritual
Karsa descends snowed, sandstone mesas along a stream
He felt fatigued and nearly collapsing but stubbornness kept him moving ever towards the world-ending event of meeting the duo ahead of him

Karsa talks to Bairoth and says they have been careless with the word ‘demons’, or creature summoned to their world. Forkrul Assail, Soletaken, D’ivers, etc. are all native just as the Teblor and humans are
Karsa eventually finds a road parallel to the gorge, with faded paintings on the mesa walls that depicted bald humans in loincloths reaching their hands overhead
The towers of stone on the horizon marked the Longshan Sea on the other side
Karsa finally decides to rest on the road, nods off, and wakes up near dawn and starts to travel again
Eventually the road hugging the mesa opened up to a shelf overlooking a city half buried by landslides, Lato Revae
Ahead of him was Icarium rhythmically clearing up the landslide blocking them as Mappo Runt munches on a goat leg, the rest of the goat spitted over a fire in front of him
Mappo invites Karsa to eat the goat, that nearly ‘brained him’ falling down the cliff
Icarium simply looks at Karsa and walks off into a cave to continue clearing the rocks

Karsa describes Mappo’s appearance as impressively wide at the shoulders with hair thickly bristled like a boar, dark skinned, heavy maned, large thick canines, heavy boned face wide and flat, eyes the color of sandstone. At his side was Mappo’s bag of holding
Karsa describes Icarium’s appearance as tall, lean, greyish-green skin, lower tusk-like canines. Had a longbow, a quiver, and a sword
Karsa joins Mappo at his hearth and eats a piece of the goat
Mappo introduces him and his partner, recognizes Karsa as Thelomen Toblakai
Karsa recognizes the name Icarium but doesn’t immediately pursue
Mappo recognizes Karsa as Sha’ik’s bodyguard and they both mutually agree to not learn much more of each other and become enemies
Mappo muses at the fact that they are Trell, Jhag, and Thelomen Toblakai. Possibly only ones of their respective race on the entire Seven Cities continent

Mappo shares his assessment of Karsa. Karsa is powerful because of the Soletaken white bear pelt on his shoulders. He is haunted by ghosts of his two friends, and of the ‘appallingly numerous’ ghosts that he has slain in his short, but clearly terrible life.
Mappo thinks Karsa is cursed
Mappo shares his thoughts on convergence, and thinks one is about to happen with Icarium and Karsa

‘When curses collide, you might say. Flaws and virtues, the many faces of fateful obsession, of singular purpose. Powers and wills drawn together, as if one must by nature seek the annihilation of the other.’
Ryllandaras, whom Karsa mentioned, is wise and gauged not to fuck with Karsa
Karsa stands up, takes off his cloak, and holds his sword as Icarium tosses out a colossal boulder
Icarium recognizes Karsa not as a Fenn, but as a Teblor from the fallen tribes in Laederon
Icarium attacks with his ancient sword, breaking Karsa’s ironwood blade
Karsa punches Icarium in the face, knocking him unconscious
Mappo then bonks Icarium unconscious with his massive bone club hidden in his bag of holding

Icarium: ‘You have travelled far, warrior, to meet your end.’ Karsa: ‘If you are so eager, cease your words.’ Icarium: ‘Eager? No. I am never eager. This is a moment of pathos, I believe. The first time I have felt such a thing, which is strange. Have we known such moments as this one before, Mappo Runt? Mappo: ‘Aye, my friend. We have.’ Icarium: ‘Ah, well then the burden of recollection is yours alone.’ Mappo: ‘As it ever was, Icarium.’ Icarium: ‘I grieve for you, friend.’ Mappo: ‘I know you do. Now, best unsheathe your sword, Icarium. The Teblor evinces frustration and impatience’ Icarium: ‘What will come of this, Mappo?’ Mappo: ‘I do not know, but I am filled with dread.’ Icarium: ‘I shall endeavour to be efficient, then, so as to diminish the duration of your discomfort.’
Karsa regains consciousness at dawn, an entire day later, and talks with Bairoth
The ironwood and handle rested next to him, as well as a bouquet of desert flowers on top (LOL)
Karsa readied his pack, wore his bear cloak, and looked inside the cave Icarium was digging
The cave contained a black statue of a seven-headed hound
‘He has lived too long, I think’
Karsa continues descending
Six days later past Lato Revae, Karsa travels through a region with the most villages and farms he’s ever seen
The region has a Malazan road the width of two wagons, and ditches on either side for Karsa to travel stealthily in
Karsa comes to a village set at a crossroads
Karsa ponders upon the inequities of laborers living only a minimal existence with ceaseless toil whose rewards are reaped by landowners and those who have control over them

‘Yet the majority of the suffering had descended upon the lowborn, upon the common folk. What matter the colour of the collar around a man’s neck [be it white collared workers, blue collar, red], if the chains linked to them were identical?’
The Whirlwind Rebellion is pointless to him because it does nothing for the lowborn, only a struggle between who’s in charge
Sneaking around the crossroads village, Karsa comes upon a mass grave pit
Karsa follows Bairoth and Delum’s direction, sensing Elder powers, to a region where several barrow mounds make a circle around a large, central hill
Karsa walks up the central hill, finding the standing stones and stone ring desecrated
Karsa picks up an Imass skull, Bairoth becomes aware that it was a shaman whose skull was placed atop the ‘four cardinal stones’ before it was desecrated
Bairoth and Delum, as ghosts chained, can access this ‘dreamworld’ for Karsa to fast travel to the Jhag Odhan
They ponder that Hood must hate Karsa because the ghosts of Delum, Bairoth, and those who Karsa has slain are chained to Karsa
Karsa feels he must answer Hood eventually
Karsa enters the ‘dreamworld’ similar to what Karsa experienced when he saw Urugal
The landscape is a cold tundra, with a heavily overcast sky. Long necked birds fly in an arrowhead formation. Trampled moss and lichen were signs that an army had passed through here before.

Karsa comes to a snowy area with large boulders of ice. Hills with sandstone exposed revealed fissures with greenish ice, the edge of a warren that’s the enemy of the army whose trail Karsa is traveling on [Omtose Phellack]
Karsa only traveled for half a day and already reached the Jhag Odhan in the dream world
Bodies, both alive and dead, are pinned underneath boulders, Karsa doesn’t want to free them
Travelling further, Karsa reaches a field of ice.
Thousands of bones and withered corpses, stone weapons, antlered helms, rotting hides. All formed a semicircle around a square tower
Karsa enters the tower, doorway big enough for him, inside was broken furniture meant for a Teblor sized race, more corpses, and an iron spiral staircase
The second story had a high ceiling, all four walls held shelves of ruined scrolls, books, vials, and clay jars. A table split in half was pushed up against the wall.
On the floor is a female Jaghut lying spread eagled in a circle of stones and a stone slab on her chest
The Logros T’lan Imass army that was here tried to kill her, but could not and cast a Tellann Ritual that sealed her and will eventually destroy this core of the Omtose Phellack warren
This will also destroy the corresponding Jhag Odhan which contains the past of Omtose Phellack of beasts that would’ve been extinct otherwise
The Jaghut destroyed a scouting party of eight, but one more had escaped
(Note: Because the seven T’lan Imass failed to kill the Jaghut women, the Logros T’lan Imass were going to punish them the same way the Logros would’ve punished Onrack for being severed from the Vow
Though never explicitly connected, these seven became the renegade Unbound, the Seven Faces in the Rock that the Teblor worship)
Ignoring the Jaghut’s warning, Karsa’s sheer ‘Ignorance honed into a weapon’ made him pick up the slab on the Jaghut’s chest unleashing High Tellann flames engulfing his body then dissipated
The Jaghut asks how she can repay them
Karsa simply wants her name, for her to find him a Jhag Horse, and more of the seven T’lan Imass she destroyed
Her name is Aramala, she recognizes that he has fought the Jhag Icarium, and she wants to free the other Jhag imprisoned under the stones
Jhag’s being half-Jaghut, she teases him on what the other half of their lineage is
Leaving Aramala behind, Karsa follows the T’lan Imass army trail and exits the warren. Karsa appears on outskirts of Sarpachiya on the edge of the Jhag Odhan
Karsa descended the slope and found the region to be a quarry, a network of caves leading to vast veins of glassy brown flint enough to make weapons for an entire army
(Note: for the T’lan Imass. Perhaps this was for their First Empire)
Karsa climbed the cliff to a large cave and wielded a lantern from his pack to explore inside
Karsa finds a vast cavern, a pillar pure flint that was unable to be mined, and a knee-high guldindha (broad leathery leaves) tree
Karsa counted 22 side chambers filled with flint swords and double-bladed axes. Karsa guessed the entire quarry would be the same
Karsa approached the pillar of flint and named the Seven Faces in the Rock, bringing them to this cache of flint weapons
Urugal the Woven
Beroke Soft Voice
Kahlb the Silent Hunter
Thenik the Shattered
Siballe the Unfound
Halad the Giant
Imroth the Cruel
The Seven Unbound have been freed
Urugal’s spirit appears and manifests into physical form
The thousands in the caves beyond were interred for failing the Ritual of Tellann, but from Urugal’s perspective it was the Ritual that failed them. Karsa understands this
Siballe, the god with no Teblor tribe of her own, had amassed all the Teblor infants sacrificed to the Seven Faces and are Karsa’s army to seek vengeance against the lowlanders
Karsa climbs the pillar of flint, ignores the T’lan Imass’ way of sword crafting, and takes out his Malazan short sword
Karsa plans to one day shatter the chains of the ghosts tied to him. However, he asks the consent of his friends, Delum Thord and Bairoth Gild, to stay with Karsa as an alternative to Hood’s embrace.
Bairoth and Delum accept and they enter the flint pillar
Karsa strikes the flint pillar, a shard of flint in the shape of a spear cracks away from the pillar
Karsa leaps off with a flashy spin, grabs the flint spear, and lands on his knees
The spear cuts Karsa’s hand deep to bone, Bairoth sealed the bargain in his blood
The Unbound move to bless the spear so that it becomes indestructible
The Unbound move to make Karsa the eighth member of the Unbound
However, Karsa is aware that the Unbound had cursed him to be chained to those he had slain and thus can never be unbound
Instead, Karsa can be the Knight of Chains, Champion to the Crippled God
The 14th Army had spent weeks skirmishing with local raider tribes, but are now pursued by a tribe of 3000
The tribe approaches, wearing reptilian armor, crow feathers on their helms and forearms, black tears tattooed on their face
The Khundryl ‘Burned Tears’ had recognized Coltaine and the Crow Clan as the strongest tribe during their march on the Chain of Dogs.
They regret letting Coltaine die and are led by Warchief Gall to avenge them by joining Tavore’s 14th Army and destroy Korbolo Dom’s Dogslayers
Gall rode to Temul, handed over his tulwar, and knelt on one knee to strive to become Wickans
Not knowing what to do, Temul looked to Sgt. Fiddler who told him to stay on his horse and speak with his words
Temul accepts the Khundryl Burned Tears as apart of the Crow Clan
The Khundryl Burned Tears all unslung and held out their iron weapons, more frightening than their warcries
Warchief Gall orders for his people to prepare a large celebratory feast
Now that the Crow Clan will be forced to accept Temul’s clan with the Khundryl Burned Tears supporting him, Coltaine’s shadow still hovers over both Temul and Adjunct Tavore
The Khundryl were a part of Korbolo Dom’s forces that faced Coltaine’s 7th Army at the Battle of Sanimon
Instead, the Khundryl took the opportunity to betray Korbolo Dom and instead assert their superiority over the Bhilard, Can'eld, Semk, Tithan, and Tregyn tribes.
Coltaine and his army were losing, but the Khundryl turned the tide and ultimately rescued them
Afterwards, the Khundryl honored Coltaine, naming Coltaine ‘Blackwing’ and the Wickans as the strongest tribe on Seven Cities
Fist Gamet walks through the celebratory feast, some eating, some running off with Wickan women, to the command tent
The meat and fermented milk is likely to cause most of the army to be hindered by nausea and diarrhea in the morning
Inside Warchief Gall was splayed drunk on a chair as Tavore was lost in thought over the fire
Warchief Gall is not worried that the Malaz 14th Army has no experience, his shamans has foreseen that the 14th Army will have a long, thought restless, life forever hunting something they don’t know
Gamet doesn’t believe in divination or in patterns

Gall retorts that the very desert they walk on is a pattern. Generations of tribes existed before they did, empires had laid claim to the land before, and even the starlight above show a patterns of the past
Warchief Galls leaves and Fist Gamet soon follows
Outside, Gamet finds Cpt. Keneb following the Wickan cattle-dog Bent around witnessing it survive the Chain of Dogs and rescued by Gesler
Cpt. Keneb notes the strange bronze skin of Gesler, Stormy, and Truth who may have made a pact with a god (that’s apparently forbidden in the imperial army)
Keneb also is aware his situation makes him look like he deserted his post to save his family, couldn’t tell who to trust because people who rebelled were natives in the Malazan army
Keneb also confides for the first time that Corporal Kalam, who was on his way to Empress Laseen, was the one that helped rescue him
Fist Gamet decides he can trust Keneb and to keep the ‘old guard’ trio in the rearguard until they can trust their loyalty
Bent is a male Wickan cattle-dog. First mentioned without a name (DG Ch. 12-2) when he pulled Nil on a travois after the Malazans and Wickan warlock twins fight a Semk godling
Later on in Vathar Forest (DG Ch. 16-3), Bent kidnaps a female Hengese lapdog, Roach, from Lenestro and they become inseparable friends

At the end of DG (DG Ch. 24-3), Gesler/Stormy/Truth find and rescue the mangled bodies of both dogs after the massacre outside Aren. Truth convinced Mappo, who happened to be in the area, to help save the dogs and he obliges
Sgt. Fiddler sits by a campfire, with the lapdog Roach gnawing on a bone bigger than she is, and his squad sleeping around him who were too tired to party after raising the camp pickets
Fiddler feels that Cpt. Keneb is keeping them in the rearguard to punish them for some reason
Fiddler is thinking of deserting

Feels the army doesn’t need him anymore with the Khundryl Burned Tears joining, that he might be trying to recapture lost youth by returning to Raraku, that he joined for revenge but it isn’t satisfying anymore, and that he wished Kalam talked him out of re-enlisting when they reunited at Malaz city at the end of Deadhouse Gates
Cattle-dog Bent comes and rests next to Roach, possessive and unwilling to share its bone
Sgt. Gesler comes with a jug of alcohol, but none of the old guard can’t get drunk anymore from their ‘curse’ and feel anxiety returning to Vathar crossing where they appeared with the Silanda
Gesler knows Fiddler wants to desert, asks what else he would do, feels anxiety for being responsible over a squad of young soldiers
Fiddler used to be an apprentice to a mason
Fiddler walks off
Fiddler hears the [Tanno] song in his head, following the sound to a circle where Nil and Nether had a bronze bowl between them, yellow butterflies surrounding them
The butterflies swarm Fiddler and he hears a voice
Note: Swarms of yellow butterflies were seen before when the Chain of Dogs crossed the river

‘Bridgeburner. Raraku waits for you. Do not turn back now. I am of this land, now. What I was before does not matter. I am awakened. We are awakened. Go to join your kin. In Raraku - where the will find you. Together, you must slay the goddess. You must free Raraku of the stain that lies upon it. The song wanders, Bridgeburner. It seeks a home. Do not turn back.’
Nil and Nether have been trying to contact Sormo E’nath and are frustrated when they think it was Sormo that spoke to Fidder, and not them
Note: Sormo E’nath had died at the Battle of Vathar River Crossing
Fiddler shouts at them to stop singing, but neither of them hear it
Fiddler walks away, thinking the voice wasn’t Sormo E’nath
The sun starts to rise
The army crosses the river and finds the remains of the battle at Vathar River Crossing (Ch. 16) of the Chain of Dogs vs. Korbolo Dom’s armies
The battle was remembered as ‘Mesh’arn tho’ledann. The Day of Pure Blood’
Local tribes sacrificed sacrificed goat and sheep carcasses, hung on long poles, from which maggots were falling into the river. The trees were filled with colorful strips of cloth and painted bones
The local tribes meant it as a blessing to the 14th Army
The bridge of carcasses made crossing the river hazardous, so Tavore orders the sappers to demolish it
Fist Baralta suggests talking to the Khundryl first so they don’t misunderstand the demolition as disrespecting the ‘blessing’
Fist Gamet goes to retrieve Nil and Nether, whose faces were in the mud, to go talk to the local tribes spying on them as well
(Note: I’m guessing Nil and Nether were mourning and failing to contact Sormo E’nath again, Tavore may be upset because she views them as still clinging to the memory of Coltaine)
The warlocks were angry, but then start to sulk and do as they’re ordered
Sgt. Fiddler and Cuttle gleefully set up the munitions and detonate the detritus bridge with 12 crackers and 3 cussers
They both end up flying and look at eachother stupidly, realizing only two cussers would’ve been enough
Sgt. Borduke’s 6th squad sapper, Maybe, comes to criticize them
Cpt. Keneb and Lt. Ranal ride up to complement them, and let their squad be the first to cross the river
The Malaz 14th Army crosses the river and reach the summit in Vathar Forest, the port city Ubaryd and the Dojal Hading Sea, and the Whirlwind wall on the Ubaryd Odhan are visible
Admiral Nok was tasked with recapturing the harbor cities along the Seven Cities coast, and has retaken Ubaryd where the army will resupply before heading to the Whirlwind
(Note: Admiral Nok’s assignment must’ve happened off screen while they were still having council meetings in Aren)
Gamet and Tavore discuss whether Sha’ik will try to impede their approach
Sha’ik would have to gamble between two options (1) fighting them on the way to Raraku, giving the army experience in battle that they still haven’t had yet or
(2) letting the 14 Army come to Raraku unhindered, and thus lacking any battle experience, but also not knowing how to measure the Army’s capabilities
Kalam wakes up to a baby bhok’aral with a skin infection napping against his side
A week has passed since he gave Iskaral the ‘dusky diamonds’, hasn’t seen Iskaral since
Kalam hears singing in the wallway
Mogora appears complaining about the mess Iskaral Pust made in the kitchen, thrusts a mop into Kalam’s hands, and gets ready to grab the baby bhok’aral
Kalam defends the pup as bhok’arala gather at the doorway, Mogora fearlessly charges and chases the flock. The flock disperses as a bhok’aral swoops in and picks up the puppy
Iskaral Pust appears from the shadows, gives him some diamonds and reminds him to stealthily breach into Raraku
(Note: The plan was for Kalam and the Ashok Regiment are on their way to join the 14th Army to face the Whirlwind together)
Kalam and Iskaral Pust travel to the outskirts of the Whirlwind via warren of Shadow
Kalam still hears singing, Iskaral recognizes he must be hearing the Tanno song
Approaching closer to the Whirlwind wall, Iskaral Pust disappears
An azalan demon grabs and tucks Kalam under its belly as it runs through the Whirlwind, toward a ruined city while leaving a path of flames in its wake
The azalan demon tosses Kalam into a fissure in the wall of the city, as it attracts the attention of the Whirlwind to misdirect it away from Kalam
Kalam waits in the rock fissure, noticing layers of potsherds, remained of a cobblestone street, and a ruin of a building’s interior wall inside.  Kalam waits patiently to the roar of the Whirlwind
Crokus carried an unconscious Apsalar to a clearing where Cotillion waited, corpses at his feet
Cotillion crouched down to mourn the death of the badly burned female mage, Hawl
[Note: Hawl was Nok’s wife when they were pirates and thought to have died when conquering Malaz Isle with Kellanved and Dancer]
Cotillion thought Hawl long dead, and to find her with fellow Talons on the island with Traveller
Cotillion pulls Hawl’s talon necklace and throws it at Crokus which lands onto Apsalar
[Note: Hawl was the former commander of the Talon]
Cotillion tells Crokus to go to the Edur ship to be sent to another one of his agents and tasks them to take down the Master of the Talon
Cotillion finally has an idea of what’s going on with the Talon, but doesn’t say
Cotillion picks up Hawl, grimly amused by the way he and Crokus are both holding women in their arms, and disappears into the forest
Cotillion comes to a glade and sets Hawl down. Shadowthrone/Ammanas appears through shadows
They assume Hawl was unaware that Kellanved/Dancer had ascended
They both feel they need to stop the Talon in Raraku, Apsalar is the backup incase Cotillion’s agent is not enough
[Note: the agents are Kalam and/or Lostara)
They both take Hawl back to their home and discuss what Shadowthrone has been doing
Traveller makes them nervous and neither want to talk to him
Chapter 16 Scene 5 (Drift Avalii, Crokus)
Crokus reaches the sandstone shoreline where he ships are, Apsalar coughs awake
Apsalar recognizes Traveller from Dancer’s memories. Traveller was with Kellanved and Dancer from the very beginning, they were more of a trio than a duo
Apsalar is saddened that they have another task from Cotillion and Crokus is staying with her
Several days after arriving via Imperial Warren and laying Olar Shayn’s skull at a resting place
Lostara and Pearl are on the ruins of city, but flat-topped hills being their only hint that they’re on one
Lostara can see the Whirlwind wall southwest of them
Pearl performs a ritual to speak to an earth spirit killed nearby
They continued traveling southwards, descending the hill until night and find an abandoned trader wagon
Pearl finds the partial remains of Gryllen, the D’ivers of rats, and Kulp

(Note: Baudin and Kulp died rescuing Felisin, Heboric, and Kulp from Gryllen after the group had just climbed out of the First Empire ruined city. Gryllen later came to Tremorlor where Fiddler used Kimloc’s conch shell to destroy him)
Pearl kicks over one of Gryllen’s undead servants, Clam, who is useless to them
Pearl can sense the warren of fire had been ‘unleashed here in a strange manner’ and left a trail
They follow the trail to another corpse, Baudin
Pearl sensed that corpse had been infected by the warren of light and Hood had come to take the man’s soul himself
Pearl thinks that Baudin, Gesler, Stormy, and Truth may have been affected by the warren of light (Note: adjacent to the warren of fire)
Lostara puts the pieces together, that since she was with the Red Blades when they assassinated Sha’ik so they should’ve seen this happen. Which means Felisin and Heboric were here after Sha’ik died
They must be with the Whirlwind’s army, both who are desperate and have their reasons to hate the Malazan Empire
They wonder who leads the Whirlwind right now, and Lostara can bring them to where Sha’ik was killed

cards.h: Scene 7 (Somewhere near the Thalas Mountains, Onrack)

i.html: After Onrack swears a Vow to Trull and both return to the material plane, Onrack plugs back into the T’lan Imass matrix, regains his memories, and and opens his inner third eye
Onrack sees the land around him as it were millenia ago, before the Tellann Ritual
Onrack was a bonecaster, but stepped aside for Absin Tholai, so that he could follow his passion for painting, and painted Kilava Onass, sister to the First Sword Onos T’oolan, on a cave wall
Painting a mortal Imass was a crime. Although Tool and other clan members felt ‘wonder and awe’ at the painting, Onrack was still punished
Onrack never knew if Kilava Onass had seen the painting herself
Trull voices his concern whenever Onack gets quiet
Onrack said he was almost banished from his clan, but four Jaghut tyrants rose to destroy the land [which prompted the Ritual of Tellann]
Onrack seemed to have loved Kilava Onass, enough though he had a wife
Kilava Onass was known to have defied the Ritual of Tellann and slaughtered her own clan except for her brother Onos T’oolan who chased her away
Onrack made love with a woman in his dark cave, but never saw her face. In the morning his body was covered in dried, crumbled powder
Onrack always wondered if the woman was Kilava and the powder was her clan’s blood, but he never found out
Trull believes the renegade [Unbound] T’lan Imass were responsible for corrupting his people
Monok Ochem and Ibra Gholan think Onrack is trying to join the renegades, so they are waiting for Onrack to lead them straight to the Unbound
Onrack and Trull reach the hills where caches of flint weapons are stored that the renegade Unbound want
‘Those hills were where the T’lan Imass had broken the ice sheets, the first place of defiance. To protect the holy sites, the hidden caves, the flint quarries’
The weapons were invested with unknown sorcery that would sever the renegades from the power of Tellann and give them freedom
Onrack admits to Trull that he was severed from the Ritual for painting a woman in a cave
The painting made [of Kilava Onass] immortal, which may be her reason for defying the Ritual of Tellann and drive her to insanity to kill her own clan
[Note: The painting is why Kilava Onass is still alive, mortal flesh and blood]
Onrack always wanted solitude, back when he was mortal and now as T’lan Imass and was happy wandering alone in the Nascent
Trull notes that Onrack is sounding more human and that he’s returning home
The Tiste Liosan made camp and are unfamiliar with the land
They got bitten by flies and are annoyed by the bug bites
Malachar feels betrayed by the T’lan Imass and plan vengeance one day
Seneschal Jorrude grieves as their ‘Guardian’ is dead, Kurald Thyrllan is under atack and they need to defend themselves until their Lord Osric returns
They have been assigned to find the trespassers, ‘thieves of the Fire’ that are nearby
Icarium - an old friend of the Tiste Liosan, the Maker of Time, Slayer of the Ten Thousand - is nearby and they will seek to find him first
Karsa sits at his sorcerous, unfueled hearth trying to turn the flint shard into a blade. No hilt or scabbard, just a leather grip
Bairoth’s irony and Delum’s loyalty ‘imbued a personality to the sword’
The Unbound stand in a semicircle in front of Karsa with flint weapons of their own
Their chains to the Ritual are now broken, they are free
The Ritual of Tellann invested in Karsa’s sword makes it indestructible
Karsa retorts about all the broken weapons in the other caves, Urugal said it was Elder sorcery of inimical warrens from the many wars they fought
Karsa asks about the T’lan Imass that made up Bone Pass
Urugal says it’s insignificant, as as they have been in countless wars to hasten the Jaghut’s already inevitable extinction, and slaughtered other enemies that stood in their way
Siballe says all life share the same struggle, both mortals and immortals strive for perfection that can’t be achieved
The Crippled God, however, demands the worship of imperfection
The Unbound claim themselves as gods because they have worshippers
Karsa argues they are not gods because they did not protect, offer comfort, solace, compassion, or pity
Karsa accuses them as slavemasters, that a parent’s love is immune to imperfection
Urugal answers that the Teblor received the burden of the Unbound because they failed
Siballe says to fail is to reveal a flaw they should celebrate
Karsa answers the Unbound and the Crippled God‘s offer to become the Knight of Chains by attacking Siballe with his flint sword
Siballe and her own flint weapon are cut in half
Karsa takes all the souls of Siballe’s ghost children and vows to destroy the remaining Unbound if they ever come near the Teblor Thelomen Toblakai
Karsa is furious that the Unbound offered ‘a new set of chains’
The six unbound leave the cave
Siballe still remains on the floor beneath Karsa
‘Once, long ago, a sea surrounded these hills. Such a sea would free me to oblivion you speak of’
