Lostara and Pearl reach the Whirlwind withered and ragged
Lostara is pissed she feels ten years older but Pearl’s skin still looks immaculate
Lostara is frustrated with Pearl’s response in getting in undetected
‘Are you even capable of answering succinctly? “Do your feet hurt?” “Oh, the warrens of Mockra and Rashan and Omstose Phellack, from which arise all aches below the knees-”’
(Note: I love how even the characters can mock the ridiculousness of their world)
Pearl plans to hide in Lostara’s shadow
Pearl and Lostara flirt in their own aggressive way
The Whirlwind Wall was only six steps wide
Lostara turns around and bangs Pearl
Kalam wakes up in the fissure that the Azalan demon threw him into
He hears the [Tanno] song in his head, sung by familiar voices that never sang a note in their lives
Kalam thought the Whirlwind wouldn’t detect him if he traveled in the shadows
(Note: Funny how they all think they can use shadows to hide from the goddess controlling the Elder Shadow warren)
Kalam saw criss crossed paths leading to false or poisoned water springs (meant to fuck with foreigners) and ancient coastal bag roads that linked islands in the past
The Whirlwind revealed ancient ships and fish bones buried in the sand
Kalam reaches an ancient causeway with about 600 desert warriors marching in a column carrying wounded
There was a standard pole carrying a rib cage with two skulls at the top
Kalam realized by their absolute silence they were g-g-g-ghosts
Kalam walks up close enough to touch them
Kalam turns hearing voices and sees a vision of a sea, with ships on fire
Kalam hears a conversation between two ghosts, Kullsan and Erethal, fighting against the First Empire, the First Emperor Dessimbelackis seems to have endless legions to throw at them
Five of the Seven Protectors [Holy Falah’dan or leaders of each individual city in Seven Cities] are gone, and a sixth won’t recover after banishing a ‘black beast’
The Nameless Ones affirmed the ‘black beast’ is gone
Kalam waits until the ghost parade past and crossed the road. A tall, gaunt figure in faded black robes, a fleshless hand holds an ivory staff
Tanno, the Eleventh and last Seneschal of Yaraghatan, banished by First Emperor Dessimbelackis for allying with the Nameless Ones
He gave the Seven protectors a song to mark their last battle
Tanno addresses Kalam as a spirit in the future
The visions end
Kalam continues traveling, remnants of an ancient city evidenced by patterns under the dunes of sand
Kalam walked down a thoroughfare and hid as soon as he heard Pardu horseman appear
A Pardu shaman dismounts, twisting his ankle, and begins casting a ritual. Throwing black glittering objects that burned touching the ground and wafted an acrid smell into the air
Kalam guessed they were not apart of the Whirlwind Army
Two black hounds are summoned and immediately bite off the Pardu shaman’s head and kill the other warriors
The Hounds were not Shadow, but larger and more muscled
One Hound sniffs out Kalam and charges towards him
Kalam runs up some stairs, dodge rolls out if the way, throws the dusky diamonds and blows the bone whistle to summon five Azalan demons
Three demons attack the first Hound, two demons charge the Hound ignoring Kalam
Kalam immediately books it
When Kalam blew the whistle ‘as hard as he could’, it seems he released all of the dusky diamonds everywhere including the ones he used to buy his two new long-knives in Ehrlitan
In G’danisban, at a jeweler’s kiosk
At a dinner between a merchant with his client’s wife
In Ehrlitan, among human traffickers and murderers plotting a pro-Malazan recruiting for Admiral Nok’s ‘avenging fleet’ currently sailing the Otataral Sea to meet with 11 transports from Genabackis
The pro-Malazan person is now safe from assassination
On a coastal caravan trail 20 leagues west of Ehrlitan near the Keeper’s bone museum, whom Karsa and Torvald met
However, the five azalan demons were forced to flee and hide from the two Hounds, defeated
Shadowthrone is in shock
The Tiste Edur ship that Crokus and Aspalar were standing on ashore Drift Avalii instantly teleports to a storage room in Tesem Temple on Seven Cities
Crokus lights a lantern using a Daru fire-kit with a gel that alchemists made with the gas under the city
They explore down the dark corridor, finding bhok’arala, leading to a circular room with tombs and where Iskaral Pust waited.
Turns out he’s Cotillion’s agent.
Iskaral Pust welcomes his friends and jokes flirting with Aspalar to upset the [wax witch inside her, or he’s calling Mogora a witch]
He sends them upstairs to meet his wife Mogora
Febryl, whose true name is High Mage Iltara, had served the Enqura, the Holy Falah’d of Ugarat during a renaissance of education and philosophy
The Malazan army, under Dassem Ultor, had invaded Ugarat

Enqura commanded Febryl to collect all tomes, scrolls, relics of the First Empire, teachers, and students to the coliseum to burn the knowledge and crucify their own people so the Malazans would get nothing
In a rage, Dassem Ultor killed Enqura
Enqura became hated by both Malazans and Seven Cities natives
Febryl’s noble-class parents had disowned him for committing such an act, he unleashed sorcery that killed them and their house guards
The sorcery turned him from a young, tall, and attractive man to wrinkled, withered old man
Iltara changed his name to Febryl and escaped the city
Febryl suspects that Mallick Rel went to Aren, so that he can turn himself in, face Empress Laseen, and convince her that himself and Korbolo Dom have been working for her the entire time

Febryl meets with Kamist Reloe and tell hims the Whirlwind Goddess was a spirit dating back to the First Empire of the T’lan Imass evidenced by texts inscribed on fired clay (that survived until Ugarat)
The First Empire of the T’lan Imass had no cities or farms, but an undead army and a throne meant for a human, a descendant of their race
However, humans had a different idea of what an empire was and so they ‘betrayed’ the T’lan Imass and warred with each other
The T’lan Imass didn’t want to exterminate their descendant children, so they left, BUT they returned when the Beast Ritual of the First Empire [human] had shattered the [Kurald Emurlahn] warren
The Whirlwind Goddess is rage that broke her chains to the Ritual of Tellann long ago
Raraku had given the goddess her memories of her mortal Imass life, as well as holding onto its memories of the sea
Febryl opens a path for Kamist Reloe not used since the First Empire
Febryl intends this favor for Kamist Reloe will allow him to retake Seven Cities
L’oric senses the Whirlwind’s rage growing as the Malazan army approaches, and begins hearing a song
L’oric first came to Raraku because he thought his father Osric was here
Kurald Thyrllan was born with the violent shattering of Darkness, and had branched off to the life-giving fire of Tellann and to a mortal human branch Thyr
Tellann was powerful, while the sister warren Kurald Emurlahn was shattered twisted Kurald Thyrllan
Tellann might be his answer
L’oric opened his hidden cache and donned his white enamel Liosan armor and longsword
L’oric hated fighting and harsh judgment, unlike the rest of his kin
He departs
L’oric came to the sacred glade, where Fel Younger rested and the Teblor gods had left their carvings
A residual fissure to Tellann existed here, L’oric opened it and stepped through
L’oric comes to an ancient memory of Raraku, on a mud beach along a vast lake during spring
White birds flew (sea gulls) and a bear-sized hyena appeared from the reeds and fled
L’oric followed the hyena’s trail to a naked humanoid corpse that drowned in the lake
The corpse was more ape-like than Imass, but was taller than humans
Sloped forehead, chinless jaw, heavy brow ridge shelf over deep set eye pockets
L’oric followed the hyena’s trail further onto dry ground
L’oric figures the sacred glade was sanctified to Raraku itself
Wild cattle with mottled white and tan hides, long black manes, and stubby horns were stampeding in the distance away from seven might black Hounds
A score of the humanoid figures flanked them as if they were scavenging what the Hounds left behind
Three K’ell Hunters (K’Chain Che’Malle that had sword for arms) were following the Hounds
L’oric felt both the Hounds and the K’Chain Che’Malle were not native this realm, intruders
L’oric knew this information because Osric was a guest at Anomander Rake’s Moon’s Spawn for months, researching the sky fortress
The K’ell Hunters fell for the Hounds’ ambush. Two were immediately killed as the third fled, unpursued
The humanoids cheered on the Hounds and climbed onto the K’ell Hunter corpses
L’oric then understood why the K’Chain Che’Malle never established colonies on Seven Cities
As L’oric turned around to leave, he saw the Hounds were heading towards his direction
Unwilling to commit the crime of unleashing the Hounds upon his world, L’oric accepted that he would die here
A dragon suddenly appeared over the lake and grabbed L’oric
The dragon took him to a tower on an island, landing on its roof
Looking upon the gold and white scales, L’oric greeted his father, Osric
Osric’s tower was bare and full of guano, L’oric slightly disappointed in his reunion with his father
Osric says he was lost as the Queen of Dreams said, but prefers to keep it that way
L’oric found his father by sheer luck
Osric is here researching the K’Chain Che’Malle skykeeps to the north

Moon’s Spawn is a KCCM skykeep whose inhabitants were slaughtered by the Deragoth and was carried by a glacier over a thousand leagues before being discovered by Osric and Rake at the Laederon Plateau
The Deragoth, the seven Hounds of Darkness that First Emperor Dessimbelackis made a pact with which angered the Nameless Ones (servants of the Azath)
(Note: The rumor that Dessimbelackis became a D’ivers of seven beasts turns out to be false)
L’oric becomes frustrated at his father’s circular reasoning, might be why Rake lost his temper with him
The Deragoth had domesticated the ancestors of Imass. Some wolf packs also had done the same
Despite being dubbed the “Hounds of Darkness”, they are not Mother Dark’s children. L’oric even corrects the name to be Dera’tin’jeragoth (which is something L’oric mother would do)
Osric jokes he could only stand his mother for three days, for his son L’oric more like three bells
L’oric tells his father to come home, Osric would rather have L’oric find another demon to take his place
Osric feels Kurald Thyrllan isn’t vulnerable, the Liosan worship themselves and he was just a convenient figurehead
L’oric asks if the tower is Jaghut, Osric says it is but doesn’t know where they are and aren’t in the memory
Osric veers into his dragon form, and despite rather being on his back L’oric is forced to suffer the indignity of being held in his dad’s claws
Osric flew along the coast, over the forest, to snowy mountains far in the north
L’oric can’t recognize the snowy mountains, thinks Raraku’s memory might be flawed
Osric lands on a deep, snowy clearing near the oblivion edge of the memory
Demons come through the oblivion but don’t exist for too long
One of the demons was a dog-sized reptilian creature with four ape-like hands, wide flat head with a broad mouth, two slits for nostrils, four eyes in a diamond pattern, vertical pupils
Osric brought them here to pick a demon to use as his replacement
L’oric has a funny conversation and picks him, despite no assurances or deal yet completed
‘Eleint! Wonder. You have an Eleint for a companion.
My father.
Your father! Excited delight! Eager. I am named Greyfrog, born of Mirepool’s Clutch in the Twentieth Season of Darkness. Proudly. I have fathered thirty-one clutches of my own-’
And how, Greyfrog, did you come here?
‘Sudden moroseness. One hop too far.’
L’oric and Greyfrog return to the sands of Raraku
Osric remains in the memory as the gate closes, distracted by something and not paying attention to their farewell
Greyfrog is hungry and is amiable to follow L’oric’s direction
Despite having all the possible advantages, Felisin Paran was still terrified to face her sister
Outnumbering the inexperienced Malaz 14th Army on their home territory with more High mages
Felisin’s mind is becoming more fogged by the Whirlwind Goddess who doesn’t want her to think
Bidithal appears to warn that Heboric is now Treach’s Destriant and also put suspicion on L’oric
More talk about the Rashan/Meanas/Thyr triumvirate
Felisin commands him instead to focus on Korbolo Dom, Febryl, and Kamist Reloe
Bidithal leaves and somehow takes the scene’s POV from Felisin (note: wtf?!)
Bidithal thinks the Whirlwind will become his own warren, and he will take a position of power
Febryl stands before him to demand that he either join them or step aside

Febryl says [Felisin] and the Malazan Empire will leave, Seven Cities and the Whirlwind will return to the hands of the Dryjhna cult. Bidithal can be the High Priest, and all of the continent’s unwanted daughters will be sent to him
Bidithal accepts Febryl’s offer, Febryl is willing to betray Korbolo Dom and Kamist Reloe
Bidithal already knew if he rejected he would be dead, Febryl seems to have more power and dismissive of Bidithal’s shadows
Bidithal returns to his temple afraid
Scillara smokes and coughs a fit annoying Korbolo Dom
Febryl had arrived moments before and said something about Bidithal (her master)
Scillara feels she might be pregnant a third time, the previous two Bidithal aborted with some tea
Scillara walks out for fresh air but a guard, Febryl’s spy, takes her to a dark alleyway to kill her to eliminate Bidithal’s spies
While the guard rapes her, Scillara takes his knife and stabs his spine and pushes him aside
Another one of Febryl’s spies witnesses it and punches her face and dragged her through the sewers
Heboric appears and kills the guard with his jade tiger claw (LOL)
Heboric puts his hand on her chest and force-heals her COPD-riddled lungs and genital mutilation
Heboric takes Scillara to his temple, fully embracing his position as Destriant to Treach, the Tiger of Summer and the God of War
Fel Younger woke up to Greyfrog eating lamb that L’oric got for him
L’oric plans to send Fel Younger away with Greyfrog and [Heboric]
Fel Younger no longer wants vengeance against Bidithal
(Note: the Seven Faces are no longer there to feed into that emotion)
L’oric will stay behind to witness the convergence about to happen before following them
Chapter 21 Scene 11 (Heboric’s tent, Heboric)
Heboric smiles as L’oric comes to his tent
He tells L’oric to move Fel Younger to a camp on the northeast edge of the oasis where there’s food, water, and six horses for them
Heboric also plans to stay for the convergence, as Treach is a god of war, after all
They both are amused at how they’re fools and how they know Bidithal will receive his due fate
L’oric leaves
Leoman and the desert warriors continued kiting the Malaz 14th Army and are not close to the Whirlwind Wall
700 of 1500 desert warriors remain
They both wished they had more warriors, missing opportunities to drive the Malazan army back
Leoman feels their job is complete and they ride through the Whirlwind Wall
Karsa spends a week or more riding on Havok from Ugarat all the way back into Raraku
Karsa wants to return to be by Leoman’s side rather than slaughter Malazans
But would happily slay the evil people in Sha’ik’s camp
Facing the Whirlwind Wall, Karsa takes Siballe out of his bag just for the hell of it
Siballe says he is the Knight of Chains no matter what he says
The Crippled God was chained by the gods to dead ground. Broken and in eternal pain and suffering.
‘Then I shall break his chains-’
‘I am pleased-’
‘And then kill him.’
Karsa grabbed the shattered T’lan Imass by its lone arm and stuffed it back into the pack.
A House is just another prison. And I have had enough of prisons. Raise walls around me, and I will knock them down. Doubt my words, Crippled God, to your regret...
The heavy infantry (1st, 2nd, 3rd squads) and medium infantry (9th, 11th, 12th squads) are joining the marines (4th, 5th, 6th squads)
Keneb was promoted to Fist, Ranal was promoted to Captain
Sgt. Balm (9th) says they all know Strings isn’t his real name, Fiddler asks wtf kind of name is Throatslitter (9th)
Sgt. Moak (11th), a Falari like Fiddler, asks if anyone has heard of Neffarias Bredd a heavy infantry who killed 18 raiders in one night and 13 the next
They ask Flashwit, Napan female heavy that had thickly muscled arms, bald, bronze nose ring, and beautiful emerald green eyes. Says he kills 50 raiders. Don’t know which legion
The heavy’s sergeants Mosel, Sobelone, and Tugg arrive looking like siblings
(Note: Neither their squad numbers nor squads 1/2/3 are ever explicitly revealed so I’m gonna take the liberty of linking them)
Mosel, Kanese (Asian looking) with finger-length braids like Jakatakan pirates
Sobelone, oldest looking, female, shoulder length black hair with grey streaks, sky blue eyes
Tugg, biggest looking
Sgt. Tugg asks what Adjunct Tavore is going to do
Sgt. Gesler says Tavore’s gonna use her otataral sword. If it doesn’t work they go home
Sgt. Moak says if it fails, then they rendezvous with Dujek and Tayschrenn at G’danisban or Ehrlitan
The legendary Greymane might even be recalled from the Korelri campaign
* Neffarias Bredd, heavy infantry, unknown squad
Sgt. Fiddler returns to his 4th squad of marines gathered around Bottle, Fiddler hears singing
Bottle is sitting cross-legged with twigs and sticks in the ground performing divination he picked up from his grandma, reminding Fiddler of Quick Ben
Fiddler recognizes the technique as earth-aspected and suggests he needs more, which makes everyone look at him
Bottle takes out a doll made of purple grass and dark cloth, ‘the hand of death’ to draw from Hood’s warren
Fiddler says he should link the doll to the Rope [Cotillion] instead
Bottle put the doll down standing and concentrates making the sticks quiver, representing the Whirlwind Wall, but gives up
Fiddler puts the doll on the other side of the sticks, Bottle tries again and some of the sticks fall over
Bottle can feel the Rope, but it’s not moving the doll
Fiddler smiles, the doll’s shadow is moving which scares Cuttle
Fiddler knows the shadow is Kalam on the other side of the Whirlwind
Gamet feels guilty for failing his first engagement as Fist
Feels the voices of the dead scream at him, and feels his body getting weaker
Grub, Keneb’s adopted son, is in the tent saying the sandstorm is very loud
Gamet opens his eyes, finding himself 50 steps away from the Whirlwind Wall, voices making up the sounds of the Whirlwind
Grub says his father has a new shiny ring around his arm and goes out to find Keneb
Fist Keneb rides up to Gamet standing in front of the Whirlwind Wall, the army had been searching for him
Adjunct Tavore readies the army to breach the Whirlwind, the Fists Tene Baralta and Blistig assemble
Tavore unsheathes her otataral sword half-way, the Whirlwind opens up and Raraku lays before them
Wickan warlock Nil says the Whirlwind Goddess doesn’t want to be damaged from the otataral sword, forced to leave fate to her Army of the Apocalypse
Fist Tene Baralta and Blistig tells Gamet it’s time for him to take back his position as Fist
Keneb isn’t confident in the noble Ranal, would rather have one of the sergeants instead but there’s too many nobles in line of succession
The Fists are concerned that Tavore hasn’t revealed what her tactics or strategy is, worried that she’s made this war personal
Blistig admits he thought Gamet was Tavore’s pet but sees he’s managed well enough
Gamet slaps Blistig in the face, breaking his nose and knocking him off his horse
Gamet rides his horse over to Tavore saying he’s ready to come back
Blistig gets up smiling, Gamet asks to meet with Blistig in private to repay the favor
The sergeants gather and wonder why the Whirlwind withdrew so easily
Sgt. Gesler thinks it was to keep the Claw out to keep the war a clean fight
Sgt. Fiddler reveals that it failed since [Kalam] infiltrated it
Sgt. Tugg says Sgt. Moak thinks they won’t fight
He also reveals the truth about Fiddler being outlawed in Onearm’s Host
That Gesler and Stormy are ‘old guard’ that served as underage soldiers to either Dassem Ultor, Cartheron Crust, or Urko Crust
That Borduke threw a noble officer off a cliff in Karashimesh
Horns sound, time to march
Chapter 22 Scene 5 (Raraku, Gamet)
Fist Gamet and Captain Keneb ride together
Keneb was happy to demote Ranal, upset that he restructured the units using Greymane’s arrangements
Gamet thinks it’ll still work out, but know Adjunct Tavore lost confidence in him

Mogora yells at Cutter and Apsalar that as a woman she’s expected to cook, and they put down their spoons at the mention of collecting cockroaches and bloodflies and cautiously picking them back up when they’re for her spiders
Apsalar knows Kalam has been here because of the marks he left behind, a ‘Bridgeburner habit’
Apsalar says she isn’t surprised that Cotillion has been paying more attention to Crokus than her, because she doesn’t want to be his servant and has too many of Dancer’s memories
Iskaral Pust appears and is shocked they’re actually eating Mogora’s cooking
Crokus says Mogora is happier without him because he’s useless and he slinks back into the shadows
Crokus asks where Apsalar wants to go now, she says she doesn’t know
But Crokus feels that she already does but doesn’t want to say it

cards.h: Scene 2 (Tellann towards the First Throne, Onrack)

i.html: Trull is happy with the spear that Ibra Gholan finds for him

Trull, Onrack, Monok Ochem, and Ibra Gholan travel through Tellann towards the First Throne on Quon Tali, past many scars of Omtose Phellack within it that resulted in tundras, glaciers, marshlands, and valleys worn down to the bedrock
Onrack forces the group to a food break for Trull, or else go on without them
(Note: d’aww don’t make me ship you two)
Monok Ochem takes the opportunity to ask why the Tiste Edur serve the Crippled God
Trull says that after he was Shorn, he understand how truly vain and glory-lusting his people were
Trull beats around the bush until deciding he’ll will wait until they’re at the First Throne to tell the tale
Ibra Golan went off to hunt and returns to throw a hare at Trull
Onrack realizes he was comfortable with Trull because of his ‘ease with hardship and extremity’
Onrack feels bad that Trull’s suffering seems equal to a T’lan Imass and to ask him to dig up painful memories is callous
Trull prefaces his tale talking of balance between opposite forces. Life and death. Dark and light. Success and failure. Curse and blessing.
People are blind to the concept of balance when experiencing triumph after triumph

Trull has his campfire as an example. The fire is a modest victory to have cooked meat, but when blind to the concept of balance, people will either not extinguish it or continue feeding the fire until it burns the whole world and leads to starvation
Onrack’s soul turns to ice and is overwhelmed by sadness (Note: because he is soft boi for Trull)
The Whirlwind Wall seems to have dropped entirely
Lostara is disgusted that Pearl is turning into a simp, trying to hold her hand in the morning
Without words, Pearl and Lostara conjecture that the Whirlwind Rebellion was orchestrated by the Master of the Talon

(Note: Lostara is also Cotillion’s agent along with Kalam. Cotillion transported Crokus to Tesem Temple - now that I think about it getting the Edur ship was wholly unnecessary - to deal with the Master of the Talon)
Lostara brings up Pearl might be interfering with plans bigger than him since neither the Empress nor Adjunct knows he’s even here. She knows Pearl wants recognition
Lostara notices an object on the ground and bends down to adjust her greaves
(Note: Doesn’t explicitly say that she picks it up but she does)
They argue, or flirt I can’t really tell
Pearl asks Lostara what she picked up earlier, Lostara tosses her pouch then punched him, KO’ing him
Pearl picks him up, continues traveling, then drops him when she sees desert warriors escorting two imprisoned Malazan Ashok Regiment soldiers, from their uniforms
Cotillion appears, judging Lostara a bit harsh on Pearl and that he might be useful to him
Lostara gives Cotillion the object that she assumed it was his, it’s not but Cotillion knows who it belongs to and wants to keep it
Apsalar looked through a window out to the wastes as Crokus slept below, feeling comfort in her solitude
She hated her inherited skills and felt like two women, wondering if Crokus became an assassin because he was in love with the killer side of her
She loves Crokus, not his Cutter persona
Cotillion appears, Apsalar wishes he took everything and left her innocent
Cotillion wants her decision, she claims Crokus for herself and he can’t have him
Cotillion tries to be a dad
‘Love changes, aye, in the manner of growing to encompass as much of its subject as possible. Virtues, flaws, limitations, everything - love will fondle them all, with child-like fascination’
Apsalar looks at him and notices him for the first time
‘The lines bracketing the calm, soft eyes, the even features, the strange hatch pattern of scars beneath his right eye’
Cotillion is pleased with her decision because he likes Crokus too and will look after him like a son
‘You don’t seem much like a god at all, Cotillion’
‘I’m not a god in the traditional fashion, I am a patron. Patrons have responsibilities. Granted, I rarely have the opportunity to exercise them’
‘Meaning they are not yet burdensome’
Apsalar leaves
The petrified forest and snakes are a giveaway that Kalam reached Karsa’s sacred glade
Kalam checks his otataral long-knife, already brittle without seeing use
Otataral is known to be weak to heat, only being applied to weapons when the metal is cooled. Making it also incompatible or weak against Moranth munitions, specifically burners and flamers
Few people know that Elder sorcery is immune to otataral, incidentally discovered in an incident outside Y’Ghatan and kept hush by Kalam and Quick Ben
Something interesting happens when you throw magic at hot otataral
Kalam then pulls out and admires his Thelomen Tobalakai blessed long-knife
An acorn falls at his feet and Kalam looks up at the oak tree in front of him
(Note: There’s an irony here I’ll probably get later)
From tundra to plains to savanna to jungle. Various biomes exist in the Tellann warren
Trull recognizes from the furs the T’lan Imass wear that they’re more of a cold weather people
Eres, the ancestors to the Imass, lived in the terrains that this Tellann memory captures
All Eres were bonecasters, and are no more. None have been found in Tellann
(Note: These were the people that existed in Raraku’s memory that L’oric entered, that were domesticated by the Deragoth)
The First Throne lies under a city, but Monok Ochem cuts Onrack off before he could say which
They’re aware once their job is done, that the T’lan Imass will try to kill Trull
The Eres identified holy sites where death gathers, carcasses and bones gathered by predators like hyenas and leopards. The Eres also gathered their dead
The T’lan Imass fashioned these sites into gates between Tellann and the mortal realm because they burned through Tellann barriers

‘Their power comes, as Monok Ochem said, from layers. Stone shaped into tools and weapons. Air shaped by throats. Minds that discovered, faint as flickering fires in the sky, the recognition of oblivion, of an end…to life, to love. Eyes that witnessed the struggle to survive, and saw with wonder its inevitable failure. To know and to understand that we must all die, Trull Sengar, is not to worship death. To know and to understand is itself magic, for it made us stand tall."
The T’lan Imass making themselves undying breaks the oldest law of all
As Monok Ochem opens the Eres bone pile gate, Onrack turns around and sees a very full-bodied Eres woman approach Trull right before they all are transported to the mortal realm
The group are transported to a crevasse, Onrack finds Trull laying unconscious and bleeding
Onrack finds three parallel diagonal cuts beneath Trull’s belly-button, with an imprint that suggests the Eres woman cut herself the same way in the opposite direction
Onrack and Monok Ochem figure the Eres ‘witch’ stole Trull’s seed
Monok Ochem doesn’t know why, says the Eres have minds of beasts
Onrack sensed that the Eres’ sorcery transferred Trull’s mind elsewhere
Panek appears riding on Apt, wearing black scaled-leather armor and a chest harness holding dozens from weapons from long-knives, throwing darts, and crossbows
They guard the outer ward as [Minala] guards the inner chamber
Minala is the sister to Selv, Keneb’s wife. Keneb had evacuated the city Orbal when the Whirlwind uprising occurred
While traveling with Kalam, Minala proved herself as a competent fighter alongside him
Minala was married to a colonel that beat her and had a healer force-heal her to beat her again to try and shape her into an obedient wife
When Kalam safely transports Keneb and his family to Aren, Minala stows on a ship to follow Kalam to Malaz City where he has a conversation with Empress Laseen
Apt, an aptorian demon, is stalked by Ryllandaras and travels near Kalam for a time on Shadowthrone’s orders
When Apt and Kalam’s group passes a field where Korbolo Dom crucified 1300 Malazan children, Apt demands Shadowthrone save them
Apt adopts a boy, Panek, transforms his face and takes him into the Imperial Warren
While in the Imperial Warren, Apt kills a Semk godling that nearly kills Lostara Yil and Pearl
Apt makes a home for the 1300 children in the Shadow warren
Apt and Panek go to Malaz city to gather up Kalam, Minala, Crokus, and Apsalar and saves them before 20 Claw agents surround and kill them
Shadowthrone presents the 1300 children for Kalam and Minala to take care of in the Warren of Shadow
Kellarstellis of Li Heng writes:

The squad regroups and is surprised Fiddler survived being so close to the crater
The group waits for Sgt. Borduke’s squad to approach

‘The song rose and fell, and he could feel his heart matching that cadence. Ebb and flow. Raraku has swallowed more tears than can be imagined. Now comes the time for the Holy Desert to Weep. Ebb and flow, his blood’s song, and it lived on.
It lives on.’
Fayelle and 13 other Dogslayers ride down a dried up river
They planned to ambush Leoman, but the ghosts had thwarted them
A volley of arrows injures her horse which falls, pinning Fayelle to the ground
Sinn stands over her and plunges her knife in her throat, killing her old master
The Ashok Regiment gathers around her as the sandstorm heads their direction
Sinn stares at Fayelle’s body, thinking she should be dancing but feels empty, as Shard picks her up and throws her on his horse
The sandstorm rages even stronger than the Whirlwind Wall
Raraku has risen to claim the shattered Kurald Emurlahn warren
The Malaz 14th Army gathers on the coral islands waiting to be annihilated by Raraku’s sandstorm of white, billowing clouds
Raraku unleashes torrents of water transforming itself back into the sea it was
Lostara reflects on the things she’d seen on her journey with Pearl
The crucified dragon. Dead gods. A dead warren and the Kurald Thyrllan warren
Lostara also thinks about her feelings on Pearl
Pearl then suddenly appears next to her
The water settles onto the basin as a shallow sea
Lostara looks at Adjunct Tavore staring at the sea and it breaks her heart
Fiddler felt the Tanno song in his soul now, looking out at Raraku’s sea and also [Karsa Orlong] riding in the distance
Smiles calls out, Kalam and Quick Ben appear via warren
All three of them come to a tight hug
Raraku has bound them all beyond death
Heboric feels their horses have been invigorated by Treach, as their horses have traveled so far so fast and still don’t appear tired
Fel Younger and Scillara wonder what they should do next
Iskaral Pust on his mule appears, and falls off, then demands help
Greyfrog leaps towards Iskaral shouting food
Isakaral cries out that L’oric isn’t dead and bargains that he has knowledge his shadows have witnessed
Also comments lecherously on Fel Younger and Scillara
Crokus stands at Tesem Temple’s topmost chamber
Feels sad that when he woke up, Apsalar was gone. Iskaral and Mogora were also gone.
Cotillion appears, Crokus knows that he spoke with Apsalar
Crokus sees many paths ahead of him, none worth walking. He sighed at Cotillion’s hinting at a job
Cotillion tells the story of a man who failed to protect Felisin Paran
The man performed the job with such honor that Hood looked into his soul and made him his Knight of Death

(Note: This is confirmation that the Knight of High House Death from Memories of Ice Ch. 21 is Baudin. The Knight defended Coll from Korbal Broach, and as Hood’s emissary demanded KB and Bauchelain leave Capustan. He then helped them inter the Mhybe’s body in Capustan’s Temple of Hood)
Cotillion tasks Crokus to guard Fel Younger, Scillara, Heboric, and Greyfrog who are on their way to Tesem Temple. Crokus accepts.
Cotillion speaks of balance, his eyes remorseful. Crokus then understands why Apsalar had to leave, as they both loved each other
They weep
Karsa rode Havok on the coastal road alongside the Raraku sea
He sets his things down and has a food break
Karsa takes out Siballe, holding her up to the water, and asks her if it’s true that her soul would be freed if thrown into the sea
Siballe wonders the reason for the mercy
Karsa now understands that glory is nothing. But mercy does have meaning, and throws Siballe into the Raraku Sea to rest
Karsa faced his sword and smiled
Yes. I am Karsa Orlong of the Uryd, a Teblor. Witness, my brothers. One day i will be worthy to lead such as you. Witness.’
Karsa Orlong continues his travel west
Minala looks suspiciously on Trull Sengar and Onrack the Broken, a grim woman he describes her
Trull offers to tell his tragic story, Minala rejects him, but Onrack says he’d listen to him
Trull’s laughs because his audience is children who don’t understand his language, three expressionless T’lan Imass, and the angry woman
Monok Ochem, Ibra Gholan, and Onrack all felt that Onrack’s wife [the Whirlwind Goddess] has been destroyed
The T’lan Imass had tried to shatter her and imprison her in eternal darkness
Trull Sengar weeps for Onrack because he cannot
Monok:
‘Broken One, there are many things you deserve… but this man is not among them
Onrack: ‘You have travelled far from the mortal you once were, so far as to forget a host of truths, both pleasant

and unpleasant. The heart is neither given nor stolen. The heart surrenders… Monok: ‘That is a word [surrender] without power to the T’lan Imass, Broken One’ Onrack: ‘We simply changed the word to make it not only more palatable, but also to empower it. With such
eminence that it devoured our souls. Monok: ‘We did no such thing’ Trull: ‘Onrack’s right. You did. You called it the Ritual of Tellann’
Together, Onrack and Trull grieve. The balance to chaos.
Trull knows his patience will be rewarded
Condensed Summaries

Karsa Orlong wanted to imitate his grandfather’s legendary raid of the human settlement on Silverlake with his companions Delum Thord and Bairoth Gild. On the way there, they free the Forkrul Assail Calm. At Silverlake, the humans were able to kill his companions and imprison Karsa by Silgar
Karsa Orlong befriends Torvald Nom who manage to escape, but Karsa Orlong stays to kill as many humans as much as he can. Eventually he is subdued by the Ashok Regiment who also captured Torvald.
The Ashok Regiment sends Karsa, Torvald, and his Nathii slavemasters to the otataral island

While sailing to sailing to the Isle, Karsa’s prayers to Urugal sends the ship to the Nascent. Karsa and Torvald explore the Nascent, slaughtering the crew of the Silanda, fighting black catfish, until they reunite with the Nathii slavemaster who has the sorcery to transport them back to the mortal realm
Karsa and Torvald land on the Seven Cities coast by the otataral sea where they spend time with Keeper who has a tower with a huge skeleton of a K’Chain Che’Malle

Karsa and Torvald travel south to Ehrlitan, but slavemaster Silgar managed to hire local tribes to enslave them both again. Torvald lights a fire that attracts the attention of a dangerous tribe, Gral, which gets him killed and Silgar transports himself and Karsa through warrens and ends up in Ehrlitan
In Ehrlitan, Silgar claims Karsa is his slave, but are both arrested by Malazans because he doesn’t have the sanctioned slave brand. Karsa receives the shattered face tattoo.
Karsa escapes with his cellmate Leoman, a leader of the Apocalypse Rebellion and Torvald’s help with the Gral attacking the Malazan compound
Silgar manages to convince the Malazans he’s on their side and pursue Karsa, but Karsa defeats them
Leoman takes Karsa to Sha’ik and they become her protectors
Several years later and Sha’ik is assassinated by the Red Blades the moment Kalam delivers the Holy Book of Dryjhna. Felisin Paran and Heboric manage to reach them and she becomes Sha’ik

Leoman is tasked to take the desert warriors and scout the Malaz 14th Army’s position. Karsa prays to the Seven Faces who want him to travel westward to free them, and also where he’ll find a Jhag horse to fight alongside Leoman against the Malazan army

Karsa leaves Raraku, runs into Mappo and Icarium, finds a barrow where his ghost companions of Delum and Bairoth take him into Tellann to fast travel to the Jhag Odhan, freeing the Jaghut Aramala when he finds her in the warren

Karsa finds the flint weapon cache where the Seven Faces wanted him to and the Unbound are now free. Karsa makes a flint weapon for himself, and then rebel against his former gods. On his journey, Karsa realized the Teblor were slaves to the Unbound who did nothing in return for them
Returns to Raraku with Siballe’s skull
Upon returning to Raraku, he slays Bidithal, Febryl, Silgar, and two Deragoth
Having grown from the boy he once was, he announces to Adjunct Tavore that the Malazans are no longer his enemy
As a mercy, Karsa throws Siballe’s skull into the Raraku Sea to grant her oblivion and swears to be the leader his people deserve to follow

cards.h: Condensed Summary: Lostara Yil and Pearl

i.html: Pearl was disgraced because he failed to kill Kalam in Deadhouse Gates resulting in the deaths of numerous Claw in Malaz City. Thus he makes a bargain with Adjunct Tavore to find his sister in exchange information on the Talon and restore his position as a Claw.
After their adventures together, Pearl requests Lostara Yil to be his personal assistant persuading her desire to serve the Malazan Empire

They piece together Felisin’s journey in Deadhouse Gates by exploring the Silanda which has faint residue of Kurald Thyrllan and believe she was present on the ship and is somewhere on the main continent.

They travel through the Imperial Warren searching for possible gates that lead them to Felisin’s vicinity. One gate is next to an otataral dragon, and opens into Kurald Thyrllan which takes them to Seven Cities
Nearby, they find the wreckage of a battle between Felisin’s party and the D’ivers, Gryllen
Lostara takes Pearl to where the Red Blades assassinated Sha’ik Elder and figure out that Felisin must be alive as the next Sha’ik
Lostara and Pearl arrive too late, just as Tavore kills Sha’ik unaware that she is Felisin. Pearl tells her Felisin died a quick death
Pearl take’s Felisin’s body to bury her on a hilltop
Together, Pearl and Lostara watch as Raraku transforms back into a sea
Trull Sengar and Onrack the Broken
Onrack wanders the Nascent, separated from the Vow without his memories. He finds Trull Sengar, shorn from his own people. Together, they explore the Nascent, its ancient city.

They escape by contributing to a ritual cast by T’lan Imass and Tiste Liosan and land on the Jhag Odhan near the Logros cache of flint weapons. Onrack swears a new Vow to serve Trull Sengar, and his memories as an Imass return.

Onrack and Trull realize the renegade Unbound that Onrack’s people were hunting are going south, towards the First Throne on Quon Tali. Thus they recall Monok Ochem and they travel via Tellann to the First Throne where they defend it, along with Minala, Panek, Apt, and the 1300 children
Crokus and Apsalar
Apsalar’s father passed away as soon as they returned home to Itko Kan. Cotillion gives them a job to sail to Drift Avalii to confirm if Tiste Edur are attempting to take the Throne of Shadow
On the island, they help Rake’s brother Andarist, Tiste Andii grandchildren, stranded Malazans, and Traveller defend the throne against a Tiste Edur attack
Andarist dies, Traveller takes up his sword Vengeance, and takes up the duty to guard the Throne of Shadow
Cotillion then tasks and transports Crokus and Apsalar to Tesem Temple for a task, yet unspecified
Apsalar bargains with Cotillion to stop making Crokus a killer and leaves to be his servant
Cotillion grants Crokus the duty to be Felisin Younger’s next guardian
Fiddler re-enlists and joins the new 14th Army under the noble Adjunct Tavore tasked with ending the Whirlwind Rebellion
Tavore absorbs the Red Blades, Wickans, and Khundryl Burned Tears into the army as well as embracing an omen that resulted in all soldiers hanging a fingerbone at their hips
They travel to Raraku, retracing the steps of Coltaine’s Chain of Dogs
The Tanno song that granted Fiddler in Deadhouse Gates manifests in Raraku, collecting the ghosts of the land, Chain of Dogs, and Bridgeburners into the Raraku basin
Once arrived, the Army of the Apocalypse had already imploded by the schemes of its leadership
The ghosts of Seven Cities, Chain of Dogs, and Bridgeburners slaughter the Dogslayer army, the Bridgeburners as an entire company ascends
Adjunct Tavore simply walks up to Sha’ik and stabs her with her otataral sword
Some squads attempt to hunt the remnants of the Apocalypse army and watch as the Holy Desert Raraku claims the shattered fragment of Kurald Emurlahn and becomes the sea it was in its past

Kalam Mekhar eagerly leaves the warren of Shadow after pissing off Minala to do a job for Cotillion to deliver dusky diamonds to his agent, Iskaral Pust, and find someone pretending to be the Master of the Talon
Kalam arrives at G’danisban and purchases an otataral long-knife and a Thelomen Toblakai blessed long-knife

Reaching B’ridys he finds Malazans besieged in a mountain fortress, he breaks in along with a young sorceress Sinn, who is a Malazan girl being taught sorcery in Seven Cities but was betrayed by her mentor, Henaras, that’s now a sorceress of the Apocalypse
Sinn and Kalam manage to get inside B’ridys, where the Ashok Regiment has been isolated and lost their Cpt, Kindly and Lt. Pores who explored a mysterious demon in a well

Kalam explores the well and finds a demon that possessed the body of a Thelomen Toblakai that can travel when it’s blood is consumed by other creatures. Kalam pisses it off and makes it bleed, which lets it blood flow through the underground river and possess a reptilian enk’aral that drinks from the river
Kalam has the Ashok Regiment evacuate and he leaves by himself so he can face the B’ridys demon.
Kalam is mortally wounded after killing the demon, but is saved by Iskaral Pust and delivers Cotillion’s dusky diamonds. Iskaral Pust helps Kalam breach the Whirlwind Wall
Kalam reach’s Sha’ik’s Encampment and during the chaos of Raraku’s awakening, Kalam is able to summon QB and find Korbolo Dom, the fake Master of the Talon and subdue him
Kalam hands over Korbolo Dom to Pearl, a fellow Claw member, and after the chaos reunites himself and Quick Ben with Fiddler
L’oric is a Tiste Liosan who came to Seven Cities to find his father Osric who is missing
L’oric had his demon companion pretend to be Osric so that the Tiste Liosan has a figurehead that can grant them power through Kurald Thyrllan and keep the warren from being vulnerable

The demon is slaughtered by Monok Ochem when the Tiste Liosan ventured off to find people who trespassed into their realm (Gesler, Stormy, Truth) and revealed they worship Osric. The T’lan Imass knew Osric is lost to his people and decided to slay this pretender god.
L’oric enters Raraku’s memories in the sacred grove, and finds his father who was studying the K’Chain Che’Malle sky keeps. They find Greyfrog on the edge of the memory to take Osric’s place
L’oric leaves and attempts to help Heboric rescue Felisin from the Whirlwind Goddess
L’oric enters the Whirlwind Goddess’ realm, but is wounded by Korbolo Dom’s Talon’s sorcerously enhanced by mages Kamist Reloe, Henaras, Fayelle, and Febryl who successfully kill her
L’oric is rescued by his father
Felisin tasked Heboric with taking hen’bara tea to meditate and discover why the jade power of his ghost arms can destroy the otataral power within, so that she can face Tavore’s otataral sword
Heboric has a vision of scores of jade statues floating in space towards a massive red rent
Heboric wakes up and becomes Treach’s Destriant, his boar tattoos transforming into tiger stripes
Heboric manages to rescue Scillara, Felisin Younger, and leaves with Greyfrog
The group runs into Iskaral Pust who escorts them to Tesem Temple
Eventually, Heboric will need to return to the jade statues
